Dost Thou Even Steal Hearts?
by BukuBuku
Summary

“Foolish mortals!” Yaldabaoth’s shadow fell over them like a death shroud, “The sin of
rebelling against a god is severe. As punishment, I banish you to other worlds unknown!”
The whole world shifted as the black wind swirled around them, twisting and contorting to
create broken fractals in the flow of time and space. Yaldabaoth pulled his hand across the air
over them, a movement as if ripping apart the weave of fate itself.
Joker gasped as bizarre doors flickered into existence.
One, a monolithic set of stone doors engraved with an alien image, cracked open to reveal a
terrifying eye swimming in a void. The next, a glowing white shoji door exuding a strange
energy that prickled at their very souls. The third, a circular ornate gate set in the floor, the
bulging eyes at the top drank in the scenery as its gaping mouth pooled with vile black
sludge. The final was nothing more than a fluctuating cloud of black and purple mist.

Notes
See the end of the work for notes

Chapter 1: Interrogation Room
Cramped, stale, and uncomfortable.
That would be the description of the cold interrogation room he found himself in. The hard
chair dug into his back and the cuffs locked around his wrists were bound to the table, a few
experimental tugs did nothing to soothe his sore wrists. Honestly, he would prefer his cell in
the Velvet Room compared to this hole. He glanced at the one-way mirror on the opposite
wall and grinned. There were eyes on the other side of that mirror, he dearly hoped that they
were unsettled by his appearance.
His hair, while not that surprising, was a ruffled, curly mess. Grime and dust stained his face,
and there was a spider webbing crack in his mask, right underneath his left eye. Despite
everything, his costume remained mostly intact, except his shoulder still burned from the
bullet wound. The police didn’t seem to care about it, but they at least had the decency to
wrap it up in gauze, he ignored the crimson splotch that stained it.
A simple Dia would have him all fixed up in no time, yet he couldn’t breach the strange fog
that clouded his mind when he called upon his persona. They were distant and slipped
through his fingers like smoke whenever he tried to reach them.
The chains around his wrist clinked when he threw his head back with a sigh. Had it been
seconds?
Minutes?
Hours?
That had passed since they threw him in here? He had lost count.
Suddenly, his heart skipped a beat as the door swung open and two people stepped inside.
One, a plain-looking detective in a brown trench coat, and two, a cat-headed police officer. It
was a strange sight.
Things hadn’t made sense since their arrival, so he plastered on a confident smirk as the
detective took the seat opposite of him. A thin folder was set on the table and the detective
dug a small notebook and pen from his coat pocket. He looked exhausted, but there was a
kind smile on his face.
“We’ll try to keep this short. My name is Tsukauchi Naomasa.” The detective said, “We
haven’t been able to find anything about you in our system. So, for starters, why don’t you
tell us your name?”
“Hmm?” His playful smirk fell into something cold, “Straight to questioning? No drugs or
beatings this time? I have to say, detective, I’m a bit touched to see someone like you care so
much.”

Tsukauchi flinched back as if he was struck, “Were you mistreated by the police force
before?”
His confidence returned like a thick veil that coated the room, he simply shrugged, but held
back the wince from the burning pain in his shoulder. Tsukauchi and the feline officer
exchanged uneasy glances, but the detective cleared his throat and plastered on a tense smile.
“We’ll investigate it if you give us names. I want to assure you that you won’t come to any
harm while you’re in our custody, and we’ll even give you a lighter sentence if you cooperate
with us.”
“Yeah, tell that to the cowboy who shot up my shoulder,” He tilted his head to the side, “And
the only person I’ll cooperate with is Sae Niijima.”
Tsukauchi and the officer looked at each other in confusion, then the detective turned to him
with a furrowed brow.
“Who?”
“You don’t know your own public prosecutor?”
“The name doesn’t sound familiar,” Tsukauchi glanced over at the officer, “But Officer
Tamakawa will look her up for you.”
Tamakawa nodded and left the room doused in an awkward silence. Tsukauchi pretended to
flip through his notebook and the folder had yet to be touched. He knew they should have a
stuffed profile, but it appeared that they didn’t have anything on him. Still, the ear ringing
silence dragged on longer and longer, and sheer boredom and curiosity finally got the better
of him.
“Hey detective,” Tsukauchi glanced up at him, “I’ll make a deal with you.”
“Go on.” Interest sparked in his eyes, and he sat up straight with his pen at the ready.
“I’ll tell you my name if you tell me what you did with Mona.”
“Mona?” Tsukauchi tapped his pen against his pad, “Oh, you mean your cat?”
He gave Tsukauchi a blank look, and the detective sighed.
“Your cat is still cooped up in a different interrogation room. Don’t worry, he’ll be in good
hands after all of this is over.”
“Oh, I’m not worried.” A small chuckle escaped before he could stop it, “Mona can take care
of himself if it comes to that.”
The detective’s eyes widened, “You really believe that, don’t you?”
He didn’t answer, instead, a smooth grin slithered into his expression.

Tsukauchi sighed as his shoulders sank, almost as if he was used to dealing with odd
situations like this.
“So, your name?”
Oh, wasn’t this the fun part? His smirk grew, and he leaned forward onto the table. The
chains ground against the metal table, but that didn’t seem to bother the detective as he
mimicked the movement.
“Joker.”
He expected the detective’s eyes to light up with recognition, or have some semblance of
surprise. But no, there was nothing of sort, just a confused tilt of the head at the infamous
leader of the Phantom Thieves. The detective wrote it down nonetheless.
“Joker? No offense, but I wouldn’t choose that name for a new villain.”
Joker reeled back, and the sudden movement startled Tsukauchi. He took in Joker’s wide eyes
and his all knowing smirk was wiped clean from his face. Tsukauchi glanced at the one-way
mirror, then back at him.
“What’s wrong?”
“You’re saying you’ve never heard of me?”
“No, I haven’t.” Tsukauchi searched Joker’s face with a frown.
Joker was about to respond, but the opening door interrupted him. Officer Tamakawa looked
troubled, and his fur stood on end as he picked up the sharp tension in the room.
“Did you find Niijima?” Tsukauchi asked as the officer approached the table.
“No. There isn’t, or ever was, a public prosecutor by the name of Sae Niijima. I even called
around the surrounding prefectures to make sure.” The cat turned towards Joker, “Are you
sure you have the right name?”
Joker’s heart pounded like a war drum and his hands sweat beneath his gloves.
“Are you sure you didn’t give me any drugs?” He forced a teasing lilt to his voice, “Or
maybe I’m not the one who felt the prick of a dirty needle.”
The officer rolled his eyes as he crossed his arms.
“So,” Tsukauchi ignored them, “This nonexistent prosecutor of yours isn’t going to help you.
Your only chance at a lighter sentence is to cooperate with us, so I suggest that you answer
my questions.”
“She’s a real person and a badass prosecutor at that,” Joker said as he relaxed back in the
chair, “I’ve spoken to her several times.”

Tsukauchi’s head snapped up at that. He searched Joker’s face as if he tried to see through a
lie, but found none. Tamakawa’s ears flicked, and he gave the detective an odd look before
glancing back at Joker with suspicion in his eyes.
“When did you speak with her last?”
“Does it matter?”
“Possibly, but I see you won’t answer that either.” Tsukauchi sighed, and wrote the name
down, “So Joker, what’s your quirk? “
What the hell was a quirk? It seemed to be a common term by the way these two ogled at
him. Joker desperately lacked information about this strange place, and he could almost hear
Oracle’s teasing voice in the back of his mind.
His heart lurched. He hoped his friends were alright, wherever they ended up.
“Information should be a fair trade, detective,” Joker said, his gray eyes pierced through the
other man, “Why don’t you two tell me what your quirks are first?”
The detective pinched the bridge of his nose, then looked at the officer. Tamakawa gave Joker
a bewildered look, his fuzzy ears twitched and swiveled like a real cat. What would Mona
have to say about that?
“Well, mine should be obvious.” Tamakawa said, “Feline mutation quirks are pretty common
in Japan.”
Joker filed that information away for later. If there were cat mutations, who knows what else
there could be? He’s only been here a short while, but that could explain the many strange
things he’s encountered if he was really outside the metaverse like Mona suggested.
“My quirk is pretty simple. It’s called Polygraph, so I’ll always know if you tell the truth or
not.”
Polygraph, huh? Maybe he could work with this.
“Well, I have nothing fancy like that.”
“Don’t lie to us.” Tamakawa suddenly snapped, “There have been several people that
witnessed the power of those creatures you control, and you even healed one of the injured
during the incident! You can’t sit here and tell us that you don’t have a quirk.”
“I’m not a liar,” Joker tilted his head and smiled, “It wasn’t the work of what you people call
quirks.”
“You-”
“He’s telling the truth.” Tsukauchi gaped at Joker, his pen hovered shakily over the paper.
“What? But that’s impossible!”

Joker smirked as he leered at the officer, “You have no idea what’s really impossible, do
you?”
“And what’s that supposed to mean?”
“Enough.” Tsukauchi glanced at the officer, “Why don’t you step out and get some coffee? I
can handle the rest.”
Tamakawa huffed, but he stepped outside without another word. Joker chuckled, and it was
worth the pain to see the detective’s bewildered look.
“What’s so funny?”
“Nothing,” Joker said, though his eyes sparkled with humor, “I just feel sorry for your friend.
A good cup of coffee must be hard to get in places like this.”
Tsukauchi deadpanned, and shook his head with a sigh. The room was quiet for a few
moments, and the detective used it to gather his thoughts.
“What did you mean when you said your powers weren’t like quirks?”
“Wouldn’t you like to know?”
“Look, kid,” The detective scrubbed at his eyes, then folded his hands on the table, “We’re
getting nowhere fast. I can’t help you unless you help me, so I suggest we stop going in
circles and get some answers from one another. Does that sound good?”
Joker didn’t respond and chose to lean back into his chair instead. The front legs hovered a
few inches off the floor, and although the chains pulled at his sore wrists, he chose to mask it
with a lazy smile.
“...Alright.” Tsukauchi shook his head, “Then I’ll ask the questions. What do you know about
the League of Villains?”
“Who?”
“The League of Villains. The ones you were with when you invaded the USJ?”
The chair landed on all fours with a solid thunk. It jarred his injury, but it was funny to see
the detective flinch backward.
“First off, I never invaded that fancy dome of yours. Second, this league needs a better name
and a less creepy leader.” Joker flared his bound hands, the blood-red gloves popped
compared to the rest of his dark clothes, “Who in their right mind wears severed hands
around their body?”
“Out of curiosity, what would you name it?”
“I don’t know.” Joker scrutinized the detective with narrowed eyes, “Maybe something cool,
like the Phantom Thieves.”

No recognition, not even a tiny spark. The detective blinked, and then his shoulders shook
with contained laughter. Joker pushed past the serpents that roiled in his stomach and
swallowed down the sandy dryness that sprouted in his mouth. Did the Phantom Thieves fall
out of existence a second time? He held back the shivers at the thought of his friends
vanishing again, amidst panicked screams and pattering rain.
“Alright then.” Tsukauchi chuckled, but his smile fell just as fast, “Back on topic, you’re
saying that you’ve never met Shigaraki Tomura before the incident?”
“Nope.”
Tsukauchi narrowed his eyes, “Then how did the League recruit you?”
“I was never ‘recruited’.”
“Okay. I believe you, but other people won’t be so open-minded, even if I tell them about my
quirk. They’ll say you had to of know their plans or at least worked with one of their
numbers, to have the date and time that Class 1-A would be there.”
Joker’s smile shook, but he kept up his facade. He could use this information for later. Right
now, however, he had to clear his name. Again. Or find a way to escape, locate Mona and his
weapons, and try to find the rest of his friends. He knew he had to step lightly here, but
perhaps he could play to this detective’s good side. Detective Tsukauchi seemed like a decent
guy, and maybe he could sprinkle in a bit of truth to get past his quirk.
“Look,” Joker pulled his lips down and furrowed his brow, “I’ve never heard of the League
of Villains, or of the USJ, or even this U.A. school before today. All I know is that one
moment I’m with my friends, the next we’re blindsided by an attack. I blacked out and I was
in an unfamiliar place when I came to. Mona was with me, and aside from him, there’s no
sign of my other friends.”
Tsukauchi stared at him in shock, “You were attacked by a villain?”
“I suppose you could call it that.”
“It?”
Joker shrugged, and he didn’t bother hiding the wince as his shoulder burned with a
vengeance. Tsukauchi’s face softened, and he looked down to write in his little notebook.
Tsukauchi missed the quick, triumphant twitch of his lips, and it was gone when he looked
back up at Joker.
“Let me get this straight, you were attacked by a villain and knocked unconscious, then woke
up during the USJ invasion?”
“Pretty much, quite a boring story without all the bells and whistles though.”
There was no way a normal detective would stay calm if Joker described the God of Control.
If Yaldabaoth taught him anything, it was that he learned to play this game, and play it well.
He was only lucky that their plan with Niijima paid off in the end, but this was different.

“Were you brought to the USJ against your will?”
Joker rolled his eyes, “That’s what I was trying to tell you before you slapped on these lovely
handcuffs and gave me an agonizing bullet wound. Not necessarily in that order, mind you.”
Tsukauchi grimaced. At least the detective had the guts to look apologetic, and he glanced at
someone behind the mirror. Joker followed his eyes, his confident smirk was reflected right
back at him.
“That doesn’t explain your costume or your unregistered powers. It’s against the law to hide
your quirk or participate in such activities without a license.” Tsukauchi said slowly, “But I
concede that you could be just as much a victim as the students who were at the USJ. Do you
want to tell me what happened before your arrival there?”
Joker snapped out of his one-way staring contest and raised a brow. This man was giving him
a chance. Joker expected the sudden whisper of Lavenza’s voice in his ear, a promise of new
power to be forged from this bond with Tsukauchi. But alas, Lavenza’s voice was silent. No
confidant was being written, so did that mean his fate was malleable?
…Or did it suggest something much worse?
Tsukauchi would never admit that this boy’s stormy eyes had pierced straight through his
heart. There had to be something more to this kid, he held an air of smooth authority that
didn’t belong to someone his age. He could practically feel Nezu’s brain going into overdrive
from behind the mirror.
Joker’s confidence melted away into a guarded mask, and he sat up straight.
“You wouldn’t believe me, even if I told you.”
Tsukauchi leaned forward, his chair creaked and he never broke eye contact. He picked up his
pen and smiled as a challenge rose up in those eyes of his, burning bright like a funerary
pyre.
“Try me.”

Chapter 2: To Another World
Chapter Notes

Edits on 3/13/2023

“So, this is the power that resists Ruin!”
“Did we do it!?” Oracle gasped in horror, “No, it’s power level—!!”
The God of Control fluttered his wings above the tower over the clouds. Joker was doubled
over in exhaustion, his friends spread out around him equally spent from fighting for their
lives, and for the countless voices below.
“Dude, it’s still not dead!?” Skull cried.
“H-how do we beat a god?” Queen whispered, “I thought we almost had him!”
“Get it together people!” Mona leapt in between Joker and Queen, “This is our final battle!
What better target to take down than a god who’s grown too arrogant!? I will see my justice
through for the sake of the people I care about!”
“Morgana…” Panther whispered in awe.
“The same goes for you guys too!” Mona had fire blazing in his sapphire eyes, “If you’ve
decided to take this world from him, then don’t compromise your own ideals!”
Fox regained his composure, hand on his sheathed katana, “What an artful way to put it,
Mona.”
“Yeah!” Panther flailed her whip and stared at the God in defiance, “We won’t go down so
easily! We’re going all out!”
“That’s right!” Noir traced the rim of her hat with one hand, and waved her other in an
elegant arc, “We’ve come too far to give up now!”
“Hmph. My control shall not bow down to Ruin, nor shall the will of the masses overcome
my power!” Yaldabaoth’s voice resonated with the fabric of reality itself, “I am the ultimate
truth of this world, and will not lose to the likes of you mortals!”
“Heh, the vanity of this god knows no bounds!” Arsene appeared behind Joker in a veil of
blue flames, black chains writhing around them, “Show this failure what it feels like to be
purged! Come, unleash my full power!!”

Joker grasped the chains in front of him, the chill of its unnatural metal sent a wave of
goosebumps down his arm.
“Wait, these readings…” Oracle gasped, “GET DOWN!!”
Joker hesitated.
It was that single second of pause…
That. Cost. Them. Everything.
Yaldabaoth’s wings shed a horrid black wind over the land. The chains vanished from Joker’s
grasp, and Arsene’s horrible scream was silenced as he was ripped away from his Trickster.
The sudden void in Joker’s heart and the cries of his friends sent a flood of terror through his
veins. The voices in the city streets died away, cut from life like the snap of a thread.
Skull jumped to catch Oracle when Prometheus disappeared in a flurry of blue ash.
“What did he do!?” Mona shouted, “I can’t feel my persona!”
“Mine is gone too…” Queen muttered weakly.
“Foolish mortals!” Yaldabaoth’s shadow fell over them like a death shroud, “The sin of
rebelling against a god is severe. As punishment, I banish you to other worlds unknown!”
The whole world shifted as the black wind swirled around them, twisting and contorting to
create broken fractals in the flow of time and space. Yaldabaoth pulled his hand across the air
over them, a movement as if ripping apart the weave of fate itself.
Joker gasped as bizarre doors flickered into existence.
One, a monolithic set of stone doors engraved with an alien image, cracked open to reveal a
terrifying eye swimming in a void. The next, a glowing white shoji door exuding a strange
energy that prickled at their very souls. The third, a circular ornate gate set in the floor, the
bulging eyes at the top drank in the scenery as its gaping mouth pooled with vile black
sludge. The final was nothing more than a fluctuating cloud of black and purple mist.
Panther stepped back in horror, “What are these!?”
“No,” Oracle, trembling in Skull’s arms, was pale as a sheet, “This isn’t possible!”
“What is it, Oracle!?” Mona demanded, “What do you see!?”
“It’s… Th-these are…”
“You have no means of escape, humans.” Yaldabaoth announced, his tone as final as an
executioner’s blade, “Accept your fate with dignity!”
The gates hummed with power as the next torrent of churning black wind descended on the
Phantom Thieves.

“Skull, Oracle!” Fox cried as the entangled pair were blown into the shoji door, it shut with
finality.
“Everyone,” Mona dug his claws into Joker’s shoulder, “Hold on!!”
“Joker!” Queen reached out to him, his hair whipping from the wind, “Take my hand!”
Joker whirled around to Queen, arm outstretched. Their fingers brushed together, but she was
ripped away in a violent gale.
“QUEEN!!” Joker shouted.
Fox leapt to Queen’s aid, and together they fell into the towering stone gate. The eye inside
narrowed with glee before it slammed shut. Panther and Noir huddled in each other’s arms as
they landed into the ornate gate in the floor, their screams going silent as they sank into the
demon gate’s black tar.
“Th-this can’t be happening!” Mona said, “Joker, we have to—!”
“Watch out!”
Joker grabbed Mona from his shoulder and jumped. A golden sword the size of a building
impaled itself where they had just stood, the impact’s vibrations shaking the whole tower.
Joker rolled into his landing with Mona tucked under his arm, their own dismayed reflections
staring back at them from the shining metal.
Great creaking metal howled in their ears as Yaldabaoth lifted the sword. Joker slowly pulled
himself to his feet, eyes wide as he stared up at the lustrous God looming over them. Mona
clung to Joker’s side, shaking like a leaf.
“What… what did you do!?” Joker screamed, his voice cracking.
Yaldabaoth’s cold chuckle echoed through a stagnant Tokyo, “They have been banished to
other worlds unknown. The strength of your comrades have been lost in the flow of time, but
worry not, Trickster.” Yaldabaoth stretched his wings, another wave of distortion rippled
through the air, “You and the Magician shall suffer your punishment together.”
Yaldabaoth beat his wings, flinging down the last gust that would silence the Phantom
Thieves of Hearts. Joker and Mona used the last of their dwindling strength to not let go of
one another, and Joker’s world turned dark as they tossed into the black cloud.
The God Of Control’s cold laughter followed Joker into the unknown.

Chapter 3: Destiny Land
“Joker…”
Joker’s body felt heavy as the ease of sleep nearly whisked him away, if only the familiar
weight bouncing on his chest would let him crawl back into the safe darkness.
“Joker, c’mon!” Morgana’s voice echoed, “Wake up!”
His eyes fluttered open to Morgana’s relieved expression. “Finally!”
“Morgana?” Joker sat up and held his pounding head with a pained grunt, “Why are you in
your normal cat form? Did we get kicked out of the Metaverse again?”
“I don’t know.” Morgana crawled off Joker’s chest, “This doesn’t feel like the Metaverse, but
you have your costume on. Can you call your personas?”
Joker sat up and looked down on himself. He still had his black tailcoat and vibrant red
gloves, his silver vest and heeled boots. Cold rain pattered down on them, and one look at
their surroundings revealed cold gray concrete on all sides dampened by the rain. They were
in an alley, though it was clean of any trash. The smell of rain permeated the air and the cold
humidity stuck to their skin.
But there was something artificial about this place. The alley was too clean, the rain too
refreshing and not hampered by the non-existent smell of rotting trash.
“Arsene?” Joker whispered.
“Trickster.” Arsene’s presence bubbled in Joker’s mind, soft and full of comfort, “We are
still here, but we are weak. Call upon us if you wish, though we’ll be limited in our current
state. Be careful.”
Joker turned Morgana’s expectant eyes, “They’re here, but they’re weakened.”
“At least we have him. Mercurius hasn’t responded to me yet.” Morgana sighed and got to his
feet, “Let’s move. We could be in danger here.”
“Right.” Joker hauled himself to his feet and dug out his phone, “What?”
Morgana cocked his head at him, “What’s wrong?”
“My phone is working like it would in the real world, but Metaverse app….” Joker frowned
as he flicked through his phone, “It’s gone.”
“Ha! As if some app can compete with my power.” Morgana stuck his nose up and closed his
eyes.

Joker stuck his hands in his pockets and watched with a raised brow. Several seconds passed
and nothing happened. Morgana’s tail twitched.
“I can’t do it!” Morgana’s eyes flew open in a panic, “Why can’t I-!?”
“Can you still turn into a car?”
Morgana whirled around to him, hackles raised, “We haven’t heard from the others and we
can’t go into the Metaverse, and you’re concerned about me turning into a car!?”
“Maybe.” Joker smirked.

Back… home?

Right now, as the police car drove off, Joker didn’t know how to feel about that.

“You think Futaba would be jealous of this setup?” Morgana asked, he set his front paws on
the desk, “This looks like a decent computer, but I don’t know much about them.”
“She would probably tear it apart and add her own little touch to it.” Ren smiled fondly as he
plopped down in front of the screen, “Well, let’s see what we can find out.”
Immediately, the feed was filled with news of the USJ, but he filed those tabs away for later.
Neither of them were prepared for the well of information. Ren couldn’t even begin to guess
how a shining baby brought forth ‘quirks’ in this world. There were laws in Japan that
forbade public use of them, but the rabbit hole expanded to a depth they weren’t prepared for.
Quirks. Quirkless. Heroes. Villains. Vigilantes. Technology that has stagnated for… 200
years!? Ren checked the calendar and his jaw dropped.
“2218, huh?” Morgana looked at Ren, eyes wide in disbelief, “And 80% of the people here
can have any combination of powers based on their genetics. That’s pretty terrifying.”
“Tsukauchi said his quirk was called Polygraph. Ironically, I don’t think he was lying.” Ren
ran a hand through his hair, “I wonder if that’s why Kaito was staring at us weird. Maybe his
quirk tipped him off about something.”
“Maybe.” Morgana sighed, “I don’t like this. We’ll have to be extra careful, Ren.”
Ren snorted, “Like we weren’t ever careful before?”
“Well, I think we’ll do a better job without Ryuji screaming our secrets from the rooftops.”
Another stab to the heart, but Ren covered it with a lazy smile as Morgana stretched, “I think
I’ll go scout around outside. I want to secure escape routes and get a lay of the land in case
that Kaito guy pulls something.”
“Are you sure? We shouldn’t get separated for too long.”
Morgana rolled his eyes, “It’s just a quick trip around the block! What could it hurt?”
“Alright.” Ren stood with a long sigh, “But I want you to come right back if you see anything
weird.”

“Yes, mom.” Morgana playfully narrowed his eyes, “Did you forget who broke us out of that
station?”
He deadpanned. “Of course not.”
“Good.”
They made their way to the front desk while Kaito looked up from his phone. His large eyes
peered straight into them as Ren opened the front door.
“My shift will go on for a while,” Kaito said as he glanced back at his phone, “So I’ll let him
back in if he scratches at the door.”
Morgana forced himself to meow in agreement. Ren held back laughter when Kaito blinked
at them several times in confusion, Morgana held his nose high in the air as he walked out.
Ren smiled, “Thanks.”
Kaito nodded, and avoided looking him in the eye as Ren made his way back to the cubicle.
He felt eyes on him, his hand paused over the handle as he glanced towards the end of the
hall. There was a flash of a pale magenta eye peeking through the last cubicle before the door
slammed shut.
Ren buried his unease as he stepped inside and sank into the cushions painted by the screen’s
pale light. Several seconds pass. A shiver ran down his spine at the unnatural silence. His
Personas had been quiet for a while. The adrenaline from the USJ and their daring escape had
long worn off, and his body felt so heavy.
This silence was too loud.
His mind flashed back to Yaldabaoth. The God of Control had toyed with them, used them as
puppets and then threw them away. He was supposed to protect everyone. They were so far
apart and he didn’t know how to fix it! The screams of his comrades rang in his ears, their
faces contorted in fear were burned into his memory.
Ren had failed.
No, it wasn’t only that…
Joker had failed. He let down the Phantom Thieves and the rest of Tokyo, they counted on
him to defeat Yaldabaoth and he just...
Froze. Like a deer in headlights.
Something twisted in his heart, and he found his breath stolen from him. The walls closed in
on him. His clammy fingers grasped the front of his shirt as his chest felt too tight. A bone
chilling cold spread through his body, and he wouldn’t stop trembling.
“Little one…”

“Big brother? Are you okay?”
“Don’t lose heart, Mask Bearer. Please calm yourself!”
“Something upset Master! Let me hunt it down and devour it!!”
“I’ll take whoever caused your distress and drown them in a sea of filth.”
The voices were masked by the buzzing static, or was it the dizziness that made the world all
fuzzy?
“Breathe, Trickster. We are all with you.” Arsene’s voice was far away in the fog, but Ren
forced himself to take a deep, ragged breath, “Good, now let it out.”
He pressed the air through his throat. Arsene repeated the instructions several times. Time
didn’t matter to one lost in their own mind, and thus nearly half an hour had passed under
Arsene’s repeated instructions to breathe.
Ren hugged his knees and wiped the blurriness from his eyes. When did he start crying? He
pinched the bridge of his nose to ward off the incoming headache and glanced at the time.
Midnight was just approaching.
“Thank you.” He muttered to nobody, “I’m alright, now.”
The flood of voices sent their last encouragements before they disappeared. Only Arsene
stayed. There was a scratch at the door. Ren set his glasses on the desk before he scrubbed the
remaining tears from his face, then stood to open it. Morgana pranced in and sat on the
cushion.
“You wouldn’t believe how many cat cafes are nearby! There are even sushi restaurants
around here! Well, of course I saw several escape routes too if we happen to—” Morgana’s
voice died when he looked at Ren. "Hey, are you okay?”
Ren smiled, but Morgana saw the exhaustion etched into his face.
“I’ll be fine.”
More silence. Ren tried to shove down the bubble of emotions locked in his throat.
“If you say so.” Morgana’s ears drooped, but he tactfully changed the subject, “Did you learn
anything while I was gone?”
Ren sat down and Morgana eagerly settled on his lap. There was an article on screen,
discussing the ‘mysterious vigilante’ that appeared during the USJ incident. Ren clicked out
of it.
“Nothing that important.”
Morgana didn’t say anything for a few tense moments, “I was able to clear my thoughts while
out walking, and I think we should go investigate the USJ.”

“Why? The security is probably through the roof right now.”
“Perhaps,” Morgana flicked his ear and looked back at the screen, “But think about it.
Yaldabaoth sent us there for a reason. It has to be worth going back there, right?”
“I guess,” Ren sighed as he ran his hand over Morgana’s fur, “I don’t remember the way
there.”
“It must be classified information.” Morgana said, “We were injured and scared, so I don’t
remember the way either. You think the school files would have something? It was their field
trip, right?”
“Are you thinking of breaking into U.A.?”
“Maybe. It’s not like we have anything else to do.” He suddenly perked up and glanced up at
Ren, “Oh, I got another idea while I was out!”
“Yeah?” Ren blinked down at him, “Don’t keep it to yourself.”
Morgana snorted, “Mercurius was right about our powers being different here, and I was
wondering if it would be possible to summon one of yours without your costume appearing.
Just think how helpful it could be to appear normal while your personas are in the physical
world.”
“I think a few of them might enjoy causing chaos without us getting caught.”
Ren made to stand, but froze when Morgana jumped up and placed both of his front paws on
his chest. He head bumped Ren’s chin, and Ren couldn’t keep a smile from his face.
“Let’s try it tomorrow. We’re both too exhausted to stay awake much longer.”
“You could say that again.”
Ren turned off the computer screen and fell back onto the cushion. A warm weight lay over
his aching heart.
“Good night, Ren.”
“Sleep well, Trickster.”
Ren muttered something, but the darkness had already pulled him in a dreamless slumber.

~*~*~*~

Kaito’s quirk allowed him to see many things.

A simple glance into a person’s eyes and he’d experience their entire lives as if he’d lived it
himself. The people they’ve met, the places they’ve been to, the food they’d eaten, their first
memories as a child all the way up to the current day. The visions were always crystal clear.
In all of the 28 years of his life, there had never been an off switch to it.
But when those two walked in…
It was like watching an old movie reel, but the edges were burned and important pieces were
lost to a weird static. He saw fantastical and impossible sceneries, and great battles with
Shadows of all shapes and sizes. The final few images were like the USJ attack that’s been on
the news and up until they walked into his cafe.
Were those two the mysterious vigilantes that appeared? Why did the cat pretend that he
couldn’t talk?
He should call the police, but...
The kid was drowning in a sense of loss, and he couldn’t bring himself to turn him in. It was
the same for that Aiba girl. His business wouldn’t last under spontaneous discounts and free
showers, but they were in desperate need of a roof over their heads. His bleeding heart
wouldn’t take no for an answer.
They could stay, as long as they didn’t cause trouble.
He didn’t know at the time, but giving this kid and his cat a chance would change his life
forever.

Chapter 7: Brotherhood
Chapter Notes

Edited on 3/14/2023- streamlining dialogue, descriptions, and adding a bit more FMA
lore.

See the end of the chapter for more notes

Makoto collected her things and put them in her bag, then waved farewell to her coworkers.
She made her way to the stormy gray skies outside, the air heavy with sticky moisture.
“Another rainy day, huh?” She whispered to herself.
She walked down the stone steps and onto the streets, her eyes were too focused on the sky to
see the figures marching towards her. A younger boy knocked shoulders with her, with
golden blonde hair and a red overcoat. His yellow eyes bore into her with irritation.
“Hey, watch where you’re going!”
There was a silver watch hanging from his pants pocket, and she instantly knew who it was.
Her job was knowing about important people, and these two were especially infamous.
She bowed her head. “My apologies, Fullmetal. I wasn’t paying attention to where I was
going.”
Fullmetal rolled his eyes and stomped away, muttering under his breath.
“B-brother!” The person in the massive suit of armor had a voice that was far too young. He
sighed, metal clanking together before he looked at her, his eyes were much kinder. “I’m
sorry, he’s in a really bad mood today.”
“Don’t worry about it,” Makoto said with a soft smile, “Everyone has off days.”
He nodded, and Makoto watched as he caught up with his shorter companion.
“Brother, you shouldn’t be so mean! She was really nice!”
“Shut up, Al! She bumped into me first!”
“Why are you like this, Edward?”
Makoto chuckled as they vanished into Central Command. She continued on her way home.
1900’s era cars, ancient to Makoto but here they looked all shiny and brand new, hummed
down the roads and people in various fashions walked the street, with the iconic blue of the

military uniform sprinkled in. Having a blue uniform of her own, the people cleared the way
for her.
She explored the cobblestone streets and made it to an apartment building just as drops of
rain pattered around her. The keys jingled in her hands as she unlocked the door and went in
with a relieved sigh. She shrugged off her blue coat and threw it on the hook beside the door
and slipped off her boots.
“You’re back already?”
Yusuke looked up from where he hovered over the table. The kitchen was piled high with
papers and books over every surface, with a full avalanche of research materials pouring on
the floor. Not even the walls were spared. Maps and glyphs and alchemical formulae were
stuck with tape.
“Yusuke.” She crossed her arms and gave him a stern look, “I left seven hours ago.”
Yusuke tilted his head, his bangs falling over his face.
“Oh, my apologies.” He straightened his hair and blinked at her, “Did you have a good day
then?”
Makoto pulled out the nearest chair and sank into it, “It was… certainly something. I actually
ran into another State Alchemist today.”
“Oh?” Yusuke raised a brow at her, “What was he like?”
“Short and angry.” She said with a chuckle, “Other than that it was a rather boring day, but an
office job is safer than being out in the front lines. I did grab a new book to add to our
collection, though.”
Yusuke’s eyes brightened as Makoto handed her bag over. He eagerly took a heavy tome out
and cracked it open.
“Have you made any progress?” She asked.
“Some.” Yusuke glanced at the intricate circles taped on the walls, “I learned ice alchemy is
rather common among the populace, so I’ll be able to hide Susanoo’s abilities under their
guise quite easily. However… the concept of nuclear energy hasn’t yet reached fruition, so
using that aspect of Anat’s abilities will be difficult when around other people.”
“How about healing? If I can’t use my nuclear spells during the day, then—”
Yusuke frowned, “That’s not a good idea, either. Apparently, healing alchemy is foreign to
Amestris. I’ve read that another country far to the east uses ‘Alkahestry’ for medicinal
purposes.”
Makoto sighed, “So using my healing spells would draw too much attention.”
“Unfortunately.”

“And I already get questions when people see my eye color.”
The temperature in the apartment fell as a severe expression crossed Yusuke’s face, “Nobody
else has given you more trouble over it, have they?”
“No, Yusuke. I’m fine, really.” She reached over and gently patted his arm, though the phrase
half-breed Ishval scum and other worse names skirted her mind. He relented and the
apartment warmed up again, and she sank back into her chair, “If I can’t use ‘alchemy’ when
in disguise, then I’ll just have to rely on Aikido for any fighting.”
“It would be a smart choice. We have to do everything we can to separate our normal lives
from our alter egos who patrol at night.” Yusuke’s expression softened as he studied her,
“You look exhausted. I made some coffee earlier. I tried to imitate the way Ren made it, but I
am no master of coffee pouring.”
“Thanks.” She said as she rose from her chair.
Makoto carefully traversed through the towers of books, and reached one of the few clear
spots on the counter. The coffee was still warm as she poured herself a cup. Yusuke tried, but
nobody would ever be able to replicate the intricate flavors of their leader’s coffee. She tried
to ignore the tightness in her chest when she thought of everyone, and wondering if they were
safe or not drove her crazy.
The first few days in this new world were…. difficult, but hearing their Personas’ voices on
the second day made things better. They found this apartment after two weeks surviving on
the streets, by some miracle they encountered a female officer when a man tried to mug them
in an alley. He wasn’t worth revealing their Personas over, but the officer came in time to
witness Makoto’s mastery in Aikido, and offered her a job in the military. It was cushy
enough to not be thrown in danger too often, and paid for this apartment and decent food.
It was the perfect opportunity to gather information, too.
In the meantime, Yusuke did what he did best. People watching, understanding the art and
culture, sketching anything he could to add to their growing wall. He painted himself as a
wandering artist and sold portraits to help with the bills.
More importantly, they were a team.
They both studied the strange force of nature called Alchemy. This force had its own laws
and balances, and it was the sole source of power within the country they found themselves
in. His art skills worked hand in hand with drawing the transmutation circles.
One thing was clear, though.
They could not be discovered. Their Personas were unique and held a range of powers that
matched what multiple State Alchemists could do. If they were caught….
She didn’t want to think of it. Makoto heard the whispers in the dark corners of the military,
learned secrets when they were out at night as Fox and Queen. They could be used as

experiments or imprisoned, possibly worse, and then they might not ever find a way home.
“Are you alright?” Yusuke asked as he sensed her unease, “I apologize if the coffee isn’t up
to standard.”
“I’m fine,” She tried to smile, but it came out forced, “I wonder how Joker would handle
this.”
Yusuke peered into her for several seconds, then sighed as he set the book down, “He would
lead us without hesitation, with that suave and confident aura he always projects.”
“Yeah. I can almost hear Morgana calling us a bunch of wet blankets right about now.”
“Or Ryuji getting impatient and just going in, all guns blazing. Ann would try and follow
along, calling him an idiot all the while.”
“Yeah….” Makoto’s mouth went dry, and took another sip.
“They are alright, you know. We Phantom Thieves are resilient and resourceful. Everyone fell
into those gates in pairs, so nobody is alone. We will get through this, all of us, in one piece.”
“You’re right.” Makoto set her cup down and stared at the largest map on the wall, “And then
we can repay Yaldabaoth tenfold for what he’s done.”
Yusuke smiled, “Exactly.”
Makoto matched his smile, “So, how was your day? Have you chased any other small
families out of a store because you wanted ‘to capture the spirit of consumerism in a strange
land.’ I bet the others will have a good laugh at that.”
“W-well that’s…” Yusuke turned red and cleared his throat, “How else are we supposed to
remember these cultures after we return home? Forgetting them completely would be an
insult. I want to the others to see the majesty this world has to offer!”
“You’re right. There are so many stories to share here. I could tell them of the Colonel that
wanted the women in the military to wear short miniskirts, or the one who shows pictures of
his adorable daughter.” She glanced at the bags under Yusuke’s eyes, her smile falling, “You
should get some rest, I can take over for a few hours.”
“...Are you sure? You’ve been working all day.”
“Yusuke,” He tensed at her sharp tone, “Did you even sleep last night?”
“I was working on an exquisite portrait of a woman I saw at a nearby cafe. She had the most
interesting tattoo of a serpent on her chest.” He looked away and fidgeted with the edge of his
sleeve, “So no.”
She grabbed his shoulders and pushed him towards the hall, “Don’t make me pull a Morgana
on you.”

“Very well…”
Yusuke slumped in defeat and wandered into his bedroom. Makoto sighed after a few
moments of silence. She glanced over to the mountain of books on the table. Reading would
take her mind off of things. She found herself reading over the same passages about the
history of Ishval several times, not comprehending the words as the sudden burn of tears
came to her eyes.
“Oh, Ren.” She whispered as her face fell in her hands, “Please be alright. I don’t know what
we would do if we were stuck here forever and I never got to see you again.”
The warmth of her Persona’s presence did nothing to soothe her heartache.
But she held on, the yearning of being reunited with her friends was one that was seared into
her very soul. She and Yusuke would return home and see everyone again.
No matter what.

Chapter 8: The Poem Of Everyone's Souls
Chapter Notes

Edits on 3/14/2023 - Streamlined dialogue and descriptions.

See the end of the chapter for more notes

The human psyche is a delicate thing.
It shifts, grows, and changes as a person experiences life, but Arsene had never seen one so…
barren. Blackness flooded around him as he floated in an endless void, dark enough to only
see quick flashes of eyes or scales or the odd feathers of the other Personas sharing the same
space.
It has been this way since Yaldabaoth sent down that black wind and banished them.
“Is big brother okay?” An innocent voice echoed.
“He’s hurting.” Arsene couldn’t see who spoke, but recognized the soft voice, “I know not
how to make him feel better.”
“Master will pull through!” Cerberus would howl it to the moon if he could, “After all, he
has us!”
“Of course he’ll be fine,” This one’s voice was dainty, yet commanding, as she floated on
invisible winds with sparkling gossamer wings, “I would never follow a weak man.
Otherwise, I wouldn’t bother being here.”
“Warch your tongue, Titania.” Arsene growled, his great black wings unfurling with a
warning, “We all swore a vow to the Trickster, ‘I am thou, thou art I’. It is a promised bond
that can never be broken.”
“I was only teasing. I would never leave him like this.” She said with a smirk, “Besides,
everything has been turned on its head since we got to this new world. We are different in this
realm, no longer bound by the same Sea of Human Souls back home.”
Arsene saw her glide through the darkness towards him. “What are you getting at?”
“We are no longer one copy amidst many in this Sea. I feel whole for the first time in ages.”
Arsene looked down at his clawed hands. He curled them into fists. It’s true. In the old world,
they were nothing but whispers and hollow shadows, only solid and powerful while in
Palaces or Mementos. Here, in this new world, they were all alive. Were they naturally
becoming more corporeal, or was there something morphing within the Trickster?

Perhaps it was this new world that was the catalyst. The energy of a brand new Sea?
“Lady Titania has a point,” The innocent one said, “The Magician’s persona said that our
powers work differently.”
“Ooh!” The bubbly one giggled, “Won’t this be fun? Who knows what we can spread in this
new world!?”
“As long as Master can be happy.” Cerberus wagged his metal tail like an excited pup.
Titania slid her arms around Arsene’s shoulders, “Everything will fall into place. Just you
wait, the Trickster will return to his normal self in no time.”
Arsene huffed, ignoring the intoxicating scent of sunshine and early morning dew as he freed
himself from her silky grasp. He missed how she pouted at him. Not that he cared about her
wiles.
“Anything can happen yet.” He said, tucking in his wings and tracing the rim of his hat, “All
we can do for now is support the Trickster with everything we have.”
There was movement, the largest of them stirred in a rustle of golden scales. Great ruby red
eyes stared down from above, a growl like a great earthquake washing over them.
“Uh oh,” The bubbly one whispered, “We woke up grandpa. Sorry, old boy.”
A snort blew down on them in a harsh gale. Arsene held the tip of his hat so it wouldn’t blow
away, his elegant feathers were ruffled into an unsavory mess. The old one wasn’t even sorry
as he slipped further into the blackness to sleep in peace, the tip of his magnificent tail was
the last thing they saw.
Arsene grumbled as he straightened out his messy wings, then turned to the others who were
laughing at him. They gained a sudden seriousness as he studied them with burning eyes.
“We should adjourn before we disturb anybody else.” He shook his head, “The Trickster is
bound to wake up soon. He’ll need all of us for support, so get some rest while you can.”
Everyone agreed before they vanished into the endless darkness. Arsene was alone. He was
thankful for the sudden quiet so he could get his thoughts in order. Is this how the Trickster
felt when leading the Phantom Thieves? The other personas had a quiet respect for him,
being the first one to manifest in the Trickster’s soul.
He was purely Joker’s other self.
Sure, the other personas teased him and pushed his buttons sometimes, but it was in the same
friendly demeanor that the Phantom Thieves had for their leader.
“I wonder where this new path will lead us, Joker. I don’t know where it’ll go,” Arsene
whispered, “But I’m eager to see it through to the end.”

~*~*~*~

Ren peeled his eyes open with a groan.
His muscles were as stiff and his joints creaked ominously as he forced himself into sitting.
The clock on the desk was a few minutes shy of 7:30 in the morning. Soft snores drew him to
the warm spot on his side. Morgana slept on his back, paws in the air, his foot occasionally
twitching in some odd dream.
Ren gently poked him in the side. “Hey, Morgana.”
The cat grumbled as he opened an eye, “What…?”
“I’m gonna shower and see what we could scrounge up for breakfast.”
“Okay.” He closed his eyes and snuggled into the cushion, “Be up in a few….”
Ren chuckled as Morgana nodded off with an adorable snore. He stepped out and wandered
towards the end of the hallway, the other tenant’s door was firmly shut and he didn’t hear a
peep out of it. He walked into the bathroom and shut the door, making sure the lock clicked.
It was clean, for the most part. Piles of miniature toiletries were lined on the counter,
alongside some plush towels.
Ren approached the mirror, he was pale and the bags under his eyes haven’t lessened any. His
steely eyes stared right back at him.
“Arsene?”
A tiny flicker of gold surrounded his pupils like a glittering puddle.
“I am here, Trickster.” Arsene said softly, “As are the others.”
“Good.” Ren sighed in relief, “Have you recovered your strength?”
“We should be asking you that.” There was a soft ruffling of feathers, “But yes. A decent
night’s sleep has done us all good.”
“I’ll be fine, but we should keep our guard up. Yesterday was bad enough.”
“Understood.”
The gold in his eyes faded with Arsene’s presence. Ren wished everything was just a bad
dream, that he’d wake up in Leblanc’s attic to find that nothing was amiss. He shook his head

muscles, he’d have to wear the same clothes but he didn’t mind. He smuggled away some of
the toiletries and a fresh toothbrush before he returned to his cubicle.

Morgana was still asleep, so Ren left him in peace as he packed the items away. He stalked

Ren opened the first cabinet he saw, and smirked.
“Instant curry?” He snatched up the plastic packet, “It won’t be as good as Sojiro’s but…”
Sojiro taught him how to make excellent homemade curry, but the instant stuff would have to
do for now. He found some spices and the tools to hand brew fresh coffee, along with a rice
cooker and a decent sized pot. It didn’t take long for the kitchen to smell of home, curry and
coffee entangling together to make his mouth water. The curry was steaming hot as he ladled

Ren turned, and froze when he noticed his audience. It was a girl half his height, with droopy

He’s seen those empty eyes before in Futaba. That same hopeless stare bored into him once
again, and he wouldn’t ignore it.
“I made some breakfast, if you’re hungry.” He kept his voice gentle with a soft smile,
“Brewed some coffee too, but I can make tea if you’d prefer that.”
The girl stared. He walked to the other side of the lounge and set the meal on the coffee table.
He looked at her and gestured to it.
“Help yourself.”
He caught surprise in her eyes as he got a second helping. He paused with the warm dishes in

eyes stared at his back as he wandered to the front desk. The man gaped at him when he set
the meal down.
“What’s this?”
“Breakfast. Take it as a thank you for giving us the discount.”
Kaito glanced between Ren and the tantalizing plate. Ren held back laughter as Kaito took
his first bite, then stood from his chair with a bug-eyed look.
“This is good!” He said, “I didn’t think we had the ingredients for homemade curry.”
“It’s actually the instant stuff, I just added my own touch.” Ren said with a tiny smirk, “The
other tenant must’ve thought so too, because she watched me make it.”
Kaito nearly dropped his spoon, “Miss Aiba actually left her cubicle?”
“Yeah.” Ren raised an eyebrow, “Why?”
“She hasn’t come out in weeks! I wouldn’t have given up if I knew she would come out for
some decent curry.”

Ren tucked that information away for later. Another mark that made this Aiba girl similar to
Futaba. Ren left Kaito with the food as he made his way back to the kitchen. The short girl
froze like a deer in the headlights, but he smiled when he saw that her plate was half cleaned.
He took the last of the food for himself, washed the dishes, then went back to his cubicle to

“There you are!” Morgana said as he sat down, “Hey, where’s my breakfast?”
“We’ll have to pick up some after we leave.” Ren set the coffee mug on the desk, “What have

Morgana sulked as he turned to the screen.
“I was looking up this U.A. school. Just this year alone they hired the #1 hero in Japan, had a
break in, and now this villain attack.”
Ren chuckled as Morgana tapped away on the keyboard.
“What’s so funny?”
“Nothing.” Ren said, despite his smirk, “I just find it weird how you can use a mouse and
keyboard when you’ve had troubles trying to open locked doors before.”
“Hey! It’s not easy to work a lock pick with these tiny paws!”
That made him laugh harder, much to Morgana’s ire. It took him a moment to reign it in, but
Morgana’s next words were like a nail in the coffin.
“Have you thought about what I said?”
Ren frowned, “About what?”
“The school!” Morgana rolled his eyes, “It would be best to get information straight from the
source. The school is currently blowing up in the news, so we could blend in with the
journalists currently storming the school gate. It’ll be perfect!”
“It’ll be a fun headline when we get caught.”
“They only saw you in your mask and costume.” He said with a flick of his ear, “I don’t think
they’ll notice as long as we don’t draw attention to ourselves.”
Morgana had a point. There was only so much information they could learn from the safety
of an internet cafe.
“Fine. I still don’t like it though.”
“You don’t have to.” Morgana said with a soft smile, “I don’t like this situation more than
you do, but we have to do whatever we can to get back home.”
Ren nodded.

They looked up a few more articles as Ren finished his breakfast. The computer was turned
off and they gathered up their things, Morgana perching on Ren’s shoulder as they took one
last look at the cubicle. They stepped into the kitchen, where the girl had fallen asleep on the

Ren ignored Morgana’s curious stares as he set her dirty dishes in the sink.
Kaito looked up from his coffee when they emerged, “Checking out already? You still have a

Ren shrugged, “We have errands to run, so we can’t stay.”
“If you say so.” Kaito stared into his coffee mug with a frown, “The discount will last for a
while, so feel free to come back when you need to.”
Ren nodded before leaving. The streets were filled with men in business suits, parents
walking children to school, and the occasional dog walker. There was a hero posing with a
whole swarm of fans blocking the road. They read that heroes were treated like celebrities,
but this was ridiculous.
“This place is a lot different in the daytime.” Morgana whispered. “We’ll have to go another
way.”
A few people gave Ren odd looks, but he ignored them as they ducked into the alleyways.
They turned a few corners before Morgana spoke again.
“So, who was that girl?”
“What girl?”
“The girl in the internet cafe? The one sleeping on the couch.”
“All I know is that she’s been in that cafe for a long time.” Ren stopped and stared into
Morgana’s eyes, “She reminded me of Futaba before she joined the Phantom Thieves, so I
shared food with her. Is that bad?”
“Of course not.” Morgana said as he hopped off his shoulder and landed on the nearby
garbage bin, “But we shouldn’t stand out too much.”
“I know,” Ren said with a frown, “But what’s the harm in showing a little kindness? We can’t
go into the Metaverse to steal hearts anymore, so how else was I supposed to help?”
Morgana studied him for a moment. Ren held his gaze, unflinching. Morgana sighed, and sat
down on the bin with his tail curled around his feet.
“I understand. So,” His tone changed as he smiled at Ren, “Here seems to be a good place to
practice.”
“Practice?”

Morgana leveled him with a deadpanned look, “You should learn to summon your Personas
without your costume appearing, if it’s even possible. I’ll keep a lookout using Mercurius’
new powers.”
“What new powers?”
“I’m… not really sure yet,” Morgana looked to the end of the alley, “It’s like I can feel the
wind as easy as breathing, as well as the people who walk in it. I couldn’t do that in
Mementos, so this will be good practice to me too!”
Ren hummed, then set down the bag of items at his feet.
“I need a Persona that won’t stick out too much.”
“In this world of strange powers?” Morgana tilted his head, “I don’t think it would be too
hard for anything to blend in.”
“Tell that to Mara.”
“Ugh,” Morgana wrinkled his nose in disgust, “You don’t have that one, do you?”
“No, thankfully.” Ren shook his head, “I sacrificed him before we faced Yaldabaoth.”
“Good riddance. Just choose the smallest one you have.”
Ren’s Personas waited eagerly at the precipice of his mind, but one in particular would be
perfect.
“Yatagarasu!”
Blue flames erupted around Ren as his costume slid over him like a second skin, the whoosh
of steady wings beat in his ears. Joker held his arm out for the Persona to perch on. Perhaps
people wouldn’t give this large raven a second look, if it weren’t for the necklace of
magatama around his neck or the fact that he had three legs.
But nobody’s perfect.
“The Trickster has chosen wisely.” Yatagarasu’s voice was as elegant as the rising sun,
“Where shall my wings lead us?”
“Nowhere yet.” Morgana said, “We can’t blend in when Joker’s in full costume.”
Yatagarasu tilted his head as if he were trying to solve an intriguing puzzle, “Trickster, can
you feel our bond?”
“Without a doubt.” Joker said, “I can feel it with all of you.”
“Close your eyes and visualize our bond.” Joker did as he listened to Yatagrasu's voice,
“What do you see?”

“A glowing emerald thread in the darkness. This is… our bond?”
“It is. Everything that I am is contained in this bond, which is turn is tied directly to our
soul.”
Joker’s brow furrowed as he reached out to this thread within his mind, letting it curl around
his hand and arm. They felt a strange tug in their soul. Ren’s eyes flew open to blue cinders
dancing around in the air. His costume was gone. Yatagarasu sat on his arm, the noble bird
puffing out his chest feathers in pride.
“Woah…” Morgana gaped, “Was it really that easy?”
“I had no doubt the Trickster would would master this bond.” Yatagarasu said with a sharp
nod, “But it was easy because I am the weakest mask. The more powerful the Persona, the
finer your control of these bonds will need to be.”
“Alright, I’ll have to find somewhere to practice with the others.” Ren said as he straightened
his glasses with his free hand, “But how did you know to do that? We didn’t have something

The raven lifted one wing in a semblance of a shrug, “A new world dons new instincts,
Trickster. I cannot explain how I knew.”
“In any case, this took less time than I anticipated!” Morgana stood with an excited gleam to

Yatagarasu glanced at Ren, who nodded and held his arm higher in the air.
“Very well. Let me be your guiding wings.”
The dignified raven leapt off his arm and vanished over the rooftops with powerful wing

stable, and he knew where the Persona was as he rose into the air.
“Follow me, Trickster!”
Ren jumped, “Yatagarasu?”
“Indeed. The skies are giving us favorable winds today. I know where we must go.”
Morgana blinked at him, “Can you still speak telepathically to him?”
He nodded, and Morgana positively beamed. Morgana leapt off the garbage bin and pranced
to the end of the alley.
“What are you waiting for, Frizzy Hair?” He said, “We have some detective work to do!”
Ren sighed as he followed after them.

Maybe this will be fun after all.

Chapter End Notes

Titania and Yatagarasu are officially added to the list, and there were a couple of hints as
to what the others could be.

Chapter 9: Crossroads
Chapter Summary

“What’s the Sports Festival?” Ren whispered to himself.
“You don’t know what the Sports Festival is? What, have you been living under a rock?”

Edits on 3/14/2023 - Streamlined dialogue and descriptions

“Do I have to stay here?” Morgana whined.

Just what kind of budget did these people have?

Morgana glanced towards the stretch of sparkling sand and waves dyed by the last blazing

Chapter 10: Phantom
Chapter Summary

The eyes in the demon’s mask flashed as other officers pointed their weapons. It flicked
one of its feathery wings, the powerful ash-stained wind knocking the weapons away
and pushing the officers onto their backsides.

Edits 03/16/2023 - Greatly streamlined the dialogue and descriptions, somehow made

Kyogi Munashisa’s office wasn’t as lavish as Endeavor's.
Not a skyscraper with marble interiors and hundreds of employees to keep it spotless. No, his
was a tiny, dirty office building with minimal staff because he had to keep up the illusion of a
‘humble knight.’
He sat in his cramped office, having just finished calculating the funds gathered from the
night before.
More than a few shortchanged him. The bravest of them were Mr. and Mrs. Xiang, owners of
a pathetic little bakery on the other side of town, but he wasn't worried. There were always
cut-purses and thieves looking for a quick and easy job. Perhaps another play could be
staged, with him as the valiant knight rescuing them, of course.
There was a weak knock at the door and his secretary walked in, a frail and useless woman
with her hair in a neat bun.
“Sir,” Her shaky voice grated on his ears, “Th-there was a report last night that one of our
proximity alarms was triggered.”
“And?”

Yamiko didn’t hate her job.
Sitting behind the front desk was easy and safe, despite the aromas of cigarettes and stale
coffee ingrained in every facet of the police station. The sharp clacking sounds of hurried
footsteps on linoleum was common, as were the disgruntled villains being processed.
But it was boring.
The officers were too formal and stiff for her liking. They kept their heads down to hide their
shifty eyes, and she was smart enough to not stick her nose where it didn’t belong. With a
long sigh, she leaned back in her chair and grabbed her nail polish.
It was one of those quiet nights where the hours stretched longer and longer, and it looked to
stay that way.
Oh, how she was wrong.
A sudden burst of heat and blue fire blew the front doors off their hinges. The entirety of the
police station froze to their core, eyes one the doors as a wave of blue fire blocked their exit.
Hungry flames licked up the walls as a demonic shadow bled into the fire. A dark and clawed
hand parted them, grasping the door frame to pull itself inside.
Yamiko dropped her nail polish in ice cold terror when the black-winged demon stepped
inside, breaking the seamless linoleum with its wickedly bladed heels. It wore a black corset
with a ruffled white tie, and a blood-red jacket dancing with the light of the ethereal pyre. Its
metal mask glowed with a demonic grin blazing in cursed fire, with long curved horns and a
top-hat nearly touching the ceiling.
“F-freeze!” The nearest officer drew his gun as the sweltering heat began to suffocate them.
“P-put your hands on your head and get o-on your knees!”
The eyes in the demon’s mask flashed as other officers pointed their weapons. It flicked one
of its feathery wings, the powerful ash-stained wind knocking the weapons away and pushing
the officers onto their backsides.
Yamiko shrieked and dove under the desk.
“C-call for back-up!” That same officer screamed from the floor.
“I-I’m trying!” Another said, “But our phones and radios aren’t working!”
The demon snorted, and spoke with a gentleman’s voice rolling in brimstone and hellfire,
“I’ll be gone long before any more false protectors can save your pathetic hides!”
Yamiko shrunk in on herself as the demon’s footsteps approached, whimpers bubbling in her
throat. Could the demon smell fear? The metallic footsteps stopped right in front of her desk.

Ding ding.
She jumped.
Ding ding.
Was that thing ringing the bell? She peeled herself from underneath the desk and peeked over
the edge. It held a clawed finger over the little silver bell, staring at her with its head tilted.
“I will not hurt you. A true gentleman would never raise a hand against a fine lady like
yourself!” The demon raised its arm and Yamiko flinched back. “But please be a dear and
give this to your boss.”
Her thoughts came to a screeching halt as it dropped a heavy suitcase on her desk with a
thundering boom rattling her desk.
Yamiko sobbed in relief as the demon stepped back, took off its top hat, and bowed to her.
Shivers ran up her spine when she saw that it had no head or body to fill its clothes, just mask
of steel and fire for a face. It stood to its full height and put on its hat. Then, it vanished in a
flash of blue cinders. The only evidence it left behind were the glimmers of broken glass
from the front door and the giant footprints in its wake, the sweltering heat was gone like a
snap of winter. There wasn’t even any fire damage.
Sirens howled outside and the slam of car doors echoed in the ear ringing silence, but it was
already too late.

Chapter 11: King, Queen, and Slave
Chapter Summary

A King meets a Queen, and a Slave is put in his place.

Chapter Notes

Edits on 3/16/2023 - Streamlined dialogue and descriptions, and an improved
sequencing of events.

Mona and Joker exchanged another glance before looking at her with equal grins.

It was a slow day for Taneo.

Silver Falcon walked down the sidewalk as if he owned these streets, as well as the hearts of
the women surrounding him. Innocent giggles and flirtatious suggestions were always
whispered in his ears. He signed another autograph for a pair of girls, twins by the looks of it.
He was about to take a picture with them when his work phone went off.
“Excuse me ladies,” They swooned as he stepped away, “Duty calls.”

He narrowed his eyes. Inu knows better than to call during a patrol, but people were
watching. He donned a confident, suave smile, his voice as smooth as silk.
“Silver Falcon here.”
“Wh-where are you right now?”
“I’m on a patrol.” He waved back to the group of ladies, who whispered to each other and
giggled. “Why did you call?”

The line went dead. Silver Falcon pulled it away from his ear with a frown.
“Sorry, ladies. They must’ve had the wrong number,” He said as he approached them, “Now,
where were we—”
“What’s going on?”
“Did something happen?”
One of the twins looked up as other voices of concern travelled through the streets. Silver
Falcon glanced up as every screen on the surrounding buildings turned blood red, the logo of
a hat and flaming mask spun in the center. The image turned to a news anchor in a red suit.
“We’ve received a shocking video and were urged to play it at this time,” Her voice through
the city, and all of its denizens listened, “I warn you that there might be graphic images, so
viewer discretion is advised.”
The screen flickered back to the logo as distorted voices warbled through the air.
“Greetings citizen of Musutafu, my name is Joker!” His voice was smooth and
charismatic, “You might recognize me as the vigilante that appeared during the USJ attack.”
Murmurs broke out through the district.
“There someone in this city that shouldn’t have the title of ‘hero’, and you all deserve to
know what he’s done.”
“Before we do, there’s one thing to note,” The boyish voice gave way to images of the attack

hidden away and masqueraded as a violent attack on the police. We would like the share the
faces of those who were in on it.”
Silver Falcon’s heart stopped as every one of his officer’s faces popped up on screen, with the
commissioner’s front and center. He took a step backwards as the people around him
whispered.

“If you don’t believe that, then perhaps this will change your tune.” Joker said, an invisible
smirk oozing through the screens, “We’ll show you the mastermind behind this scandal with
solid evidence to his crimes.”
It was like the world fell out from underneath him. Videos, photos, notes, receipts, and all
other manner of things were played on the screens. Silver Falcon, the glorious shining hero,
threatening people who cowered under his fierce scowls. The videos shown how he
demanded money from several establishments, his voice rained over the city as his threats
were known to all.
The screen returned to it’s bloody red hue, the mask and hat icon slowly swiveling.
“Well, that’s not a hero I would look up to.” Joker said with a dark chuckle, “What do you
think, everyone? Does this man deserve the title of ‘hero’? We’ll leave you to decide.”
With that, the screen went back to the news anchor, who’s jaw was dropped in shock.
“We got hacked? I…” She looked past someone on camera, then cleared her throat, “I have a
son that looked up to him, but he’s not the only one to be horrified by this. W-we’ll keep you
updated on the case as it progresses.”
The screens glitched, then returned to whatever advertisements they were playing before.
Dead silence drowned the street as several eyes stabbed into him.
“I-it’s all lies!” He yelled, the twins flinched back as if he burned them, “It’s not true! It’s…
I…”
“It has to be fake!” One person called from the crowd, “Why should we believe anything this
vigilante says?”
Hope flickered in his heart as other people agreed, but was stamped out just as quick.
“No, it’s all real!” His secretary, whom he had sent out on an errand in this area, had been in
the crowd, “I work for him! He.. he hurts me… he… always yells at me! I can’t take it
anymore!”
“These videos are true!” Another man shoved his way to the center, “Days ago he had
villains destroy my store! My... my little girls don’t even have a home anymore because I
wouldn’t pay him!”
The crowd continued to turn on him as other shopkeepers and local business owners joined
in, bearing down all around him in a seething wave of rage.
“You call yourself a hero!?”
“How many lives did you ruin to satisfy yourself!?”
“You’re a monster, not a hero!”
“How could they let someone like this pass in a hero school?”

“I…” Silver Falcon was suddenly dizzy, his hands trembled, “They’re all lies, I tell you!
Please…”
He looked up, and his whole body flooding with ice. Within the yelling crowd was a boy with
steely silver eyes hidden behind thick glasses. A cat was hanging from his shoulder, looking
as proud as a mighty lion. The both of them… were smirking right at him.
His face twisted, “So it was you!”
Silver Falcon drew his beautiful sword and approached the boy. He shed the confidence and
adopted the image of a terrified child as if it were a second skin. The cat mewled pathetically
and cowered in the boy’s hair.
“P-please! Please d-don’t hurt me a-anymore just because I-I’m quirkless!”
Silver Falcon froze. That single line drove the crowd insane. A sharp pain bloomed across his
face, he reached up to feel blood dripping down his forehead. The rock bounced off the
pavement as he looked to the little girl, no older than five, who had thrown it.
“Leave him alone!” She said, fists clenched and tears streaked down his cheeks, “Y-You took
my daddy’s store away! I-I won’t let you hurt anyone else!”
“Is that all you do!? Pick on the weak so that they can’t fight back!?” A woman, who he had
just signed an autograph for, threw the paper down and stomped on it, “I hate people like
you!”
The crowd threw rocks, trash, anything they could get their hands on. He ducked and weaved
with agile grace, but it didn’t stop. Hatred curled around his heart as he turned to the boy and
his cat. How could they not see the deceiving gleam in the boy’s eyes!? A ragged battle cry
ripped from his throat and the crowd screamed as he raised his sword to cut the boy down.
“Lacquered Chain Prison!”
He was bound by an explosion of wooden roots, his marvelous sword dropped from his grasp
as he thrashed like a wild animal. The crowd cheered as Kamui Woods slowly approached,
his eyes equally wide in both revulsion and shock.
“Kyogi Munashisa, you are under arrest for various crimes as well as attacking civilians.”
The hero said, “Many of your cohorts are already in custody, so just come quietly before you
lose the last shred of your dignity!”
Silver Falcon went limp until the police cuffed him and dragged him to a car. He stared at the
boy and his cat as they were comforted by Kamui Woods, who had a strong hand on the
trembling boy’s shoulder. The car door slammed shut with the finality of his wings being
clipped.
The boy’s confident silver eyes were forever seared into his mind.

but I’ll have to charge you.”
Giran stroked his goatee thoughtfully, “How about I try one and I’ll pay double for them, if
you’re telling the truth.”
Joker waived a hand, “Deal.”
Giran took the immaculate pearl and broke it in between his fingers. Dancing light streams
swirled around him as every fibre of his being charged with energy. Giran stood there, jaw
dropped. He forced a cough. His lungs were so clear and the overwhelming cravings for
tobacco were all but gone. The headache pestering him all day miraculously vanished.
“Joker.” Giran grabbed the cigarette from his lips and turned to Joker in shock, “Where did
you get this stuff?”
“Around. A bank floating in the sky, a perverted castle, an art museum curated by a tacky
gold shogun.” Joker stepped around the table, his footsteps splashing with brilliant colors,
“It’s amazing what treasures people will leave unattended.”
Giran chuckled, which slowly turned into gut busting laughter. He had to take deep breaths
and wiped the tears from his eyes.
“I like your sense of humor. You have some good stock here, I’ll give you that.” Giran’s eyes
caught an item hanging from Joker’s belt. “What’s that?”
“It’s not for sale.” Joker said with a frown.
“Can I look at it? I’m a collector of curiosities, and I’ve never seen anything like it.”
Joker narrowed his eyes, but relented.
Raw power filled him the moment he touched the smooth crystalline skull. He felt invincible,
as if he could punch straight through concrete or run a marathon without breaking a sweat.
The details of the crystal skull were so perfect that it couldn’t have been crafted by a human,
it’s mesmerizing colors kept shifting in the light. Joker cleared his throat and Giran hesitantly
handed it back.
“That alone would net you a fortune.”
“Maybe.” Joker reattached the Crystal Skull to his belt, “But it’s not for sale.”

“I can see why.” Giran nodded to the table of goods in between them, “I’ll give you a
hundred and fifty thousand yen for the lot.”
“A hundred and fifty? My last fence would’ve given me a lot more.”
Curiosity peaked on Giran’s face, “Oh? Then why don’t you go to him?”
“He’s out of town right now, but I could wait for him to get back and take these items with
me.” Another smooth grin split Joker’s face, “But I’ll charge you for using a Bead.”
“Heh, I can see you’re driving a hard bargain.” Giran sighed wistfully, “Right after my own
damn heart. Fine then, one-sixty.”
“Two hundred.”
“Two hundred?” Giran’s eyes flashed with amusement, “How about one-seventy?”
“One-ninety.”
“I’ll meet you in the middle and go one-eighty, but I can’t do more than that.”
“I suppose that’s good enough.” Joker dug out a piece of paper from his pocket, “Wire the
money into these accounts. It doesn’t matter how much goes into what account, just make
sure that its the full amount overall.”
Giran blinked curiously at it. “Alright, then.”
The man stepped away as he got out his phone and held it up to his ear.
“How goes it, Trickster?” Yatagarasu asked.
“Better than I thought it would.” Joker studied Giran, “How’s Morgana doing?”
“See for yourself. We’re above you.”
He looked up to one of the grimy windows where their shadows were silhouetted against it.
Morgana nudged the window open and looked down at him with a tilt of his head. Joker bit
his lip to stop himself from laughing.
“Tell him we’ll have enough for the ticket and some good sushi tonight. We deserve a reward
for the whole Silver Falcon fiasco.”
Yatagarasu leaned in to whisper in the cat’s ear. Morgana beamed and licked his chops.
Suddenly, his phone gave off a few pings, and he dug it out to see that the accounts were
filled with the agreed upon amount of 180,000 yen.
Joker smirked as he turned to Giran, who had just hung up his phone. “Pleasure doing
business with you.”

“Pleasure was all mine, kid.” Giran threw down his cigarette and stomped it out, “I hope
you’ll call me when you’ve ‘obtained’ more goods.”
“Will do.” Joker walked towards the door and waved, “See ya.”
Joker stepped out into the night air. He was glad to be out of that filthy place, but the briny
smell from the nearby shipyard didn’t do it justice, either.
“You want us to come down?”
“I’ll come up, just wait there.”
It was child’s play to hop up the nearby crates and onto the rooftop.
Morgana jumped on his shoulder, “When are we getting sushi!?”
“That’s the first thing you ask me when I risk my life to get us money?” Joker put a hand
over his heart in mock injury, “Morgana, I’m so disappointed.”
“You’ll get over it.” Morgana swatted his tail over the back of Joker’s head, “But let’s not
stick around here too much longer.”
“Good idea.”
Yatagarasu took off into the dark sky, nobody was around to witness the figures dart across
over the rooftops as easy as breathing, Morgana only spoke when the stars dotted the sky and
they were an entire district away from shady businessmen.
“Why did you only sell him a tiny portion of what we had?” He asked, “Wouldn’t we have
gotten more money?”
Joker stopped on a rooftop of an apartment building. Yatagarasu flew in a wide circle
overhead as he sat on the edge of the building with a long sigh, his legs dangled from the
sheer drop. The stretch of shimmering city lights and nightly traffic was beautiful, if
anything.
“It’s simple supply and demand.” He said as Morgana hopped off of his shoulder, “Their
value wouldn’t be as high if there were a bunch of them out there, so when I limit the number
and get more demand for them, the higher their price is.”
“Ohh, I get it!” He swished his tail back and forth, “Can we buy sushi now?”
“The Sports Festival ticket comes first.” Joker said as he got out his phone.
“Seventy thousand yen, right?” Morgana sat beside him and looked out into the city, the
lights speckling Morgana’s eyes like galaxies, “No wonder that school is so huge, getting
sales like that for one ticket.”
Joker sighed as he placed his order for one ticket to be delivered tomorrow by mail. Aiba set
up an anonymous P.O. box not too far from the Raven’s Nest for them. 110,000 yen left. It

felt nice to have some real finances again.
“We still have plenty for sushi.” Joker stated, “We’ll have to get some for Kaito and Aiba
too.”
“Can I get tuna!? I like tuna!” Morgana gave Joker the most adorable expression he could
muster, complete with big eyes and saggy ears, “I looooove tuna. Did I mention that I want
tuna, Joker?”
“Nope, not once.” Joker laughed and pat Morgana’s head, “I’ll look up a nearby restaurant so
we can get your precious tuna.”
“Yes!”
Morgana hummed a happy tune and bounced happily on his front paws. Joker exited the
browser while Morgana was distracted. The Phantom Thief chat room was still vacant, not a
single word had been sent by the others. It was like a knife twisting through his heart.
“Trickster…”
“I’m fine, Yatagarasu.”
Of course, the bird’s doubts trickled down his spine, but he said no more.
He didn’t know what prompted him to type all of a sudden.
