FANART!!

~*~*~*~

The holographic map purred, bringing the buildings and streets of Karakura Town to life.
Energy signatures around the city glittered under Oracle’s eyes like jewels. She fiddled with
the dials on the side of her mask, watching as a golden marble wreathed in lightning left the
convenience store.
Her stomach gurgled and she lifted the mask off of her face with a sigh, scrubbing at her eyes
and blinking wearily at the dingy warehouse. Oracle’s ‘room’ was nothing more than a few
boxes piled together and covered with a tarp to help keep out the cold, which easily cut into
the warehouse because the thin rusted walls were full of holes. The smell of iron and rust
always hit her in the face, like sucking on an old penny.
Or the smell of blood…
So much blood…
An alarm piercing her ears brought her out of her spell, and she threw on her mask to see a
blinking red dot in the middle of town. A few seconds later a blood curdling roar echoed
across the city.
“It’s another one of those monsters!” Ryuji’s yellow marble wavered under a wave of strange
pressure, “I want to go get a look at it.”

“Skull, no!” She snapped, “There are already other energy signatures converging on it and I
don’t want them to spot you. We’re trying to stay hidden, remember?”
“A quick peek won’t hurt anything.”
“Please, just leave it alone?” She grasped her stomach as it grumbled, “We haven’t eaten
since yesterday. I feel like my stomach is going to turn inside out!”
“I… Okay, okay. They had some of those animal faced meat buns that you like. I got a few
extra for you.”
“Thanks.” A tiny smile quirked her lips.
“Don’t mention it. I gotta take care of Ren-Ren’s adopted little sis, right?”
Her cheeks burned at the same time her heart hurt. It was a feeling that was as foreign as it
was familiar, to have that yearning chasm of coiling emotions rising and falling like the tide.
One misstep and her emotions would gouge her like blades of glass. She missed Ren and
Sojiro and the others so much.
Skull prevented her from spiraling, but sometimes he was a little too loud or swore too much.
But he missed them too. The bags accumulated under his eyes. Sometimes his temper was
shorter than normal or he would spend nights pacing the warehouse.
Another alarm rang in her ears. She gasped as ice trailed down her spine, the hairs on the
back of her neck standing straight up.
Oracle swallowed thickly as her hands trembled, “Skull…somebody’s in the warehouse…”
“What!?” His golden orb shot off towards the outskirts of town, lightning crackling around
his soul, “Hang on, I’ll be there soon!”
“Oooh, not many people can sense my presence when I don’t want them to. Color me
impressed, little lady.”
There was a swish of air. She dispelled the map and saw a pair of sandalled feet a few meters
away from her makeshift hovel. She slowly looked up, glancing over his billowing black
haori and green shihakusho to stare at his face. Messy blonde hair spilled out from
underneath a striped bucket hat, his slate gray eyes stared straight into her soul.
“You can come out you know!” He produced a fan from his sleeve and gingerly waved it at
her, “I won’t bite.”
Oracle slowly crawled out. A pit fell into her stomach as her mask read his staggering power
levels, it was one of the highest readings yet! Why didn’t she sense him earlier?
Her hands fidgeted together, but she forced a brave front,“Who are you?”
“Urahara Kisuke, a humble shop owner.” He smiled like a fox as he studied her, “But the real
question is, who are you?”

She didn’t answer, her heart pounding too loud in her ears.
A strange fuzziness permeated the warehouse. Urahara flipped his fan closed and plucked
something from the air as if it were a delicate flower. Her chest tightened as the air was
sucked out of her, there was a tugging sensation in her chest as he held a ribbon between his
fingers. It was pitch black, with jagged lines reminiscent to the inner workings of a computer.
Prometheus’ snarl trembled the warehouse and slashed at this man’s power. The ribbon
glitched out of his hand and vanished. His eyes sharpened like a blade to cover his surprise.
“Your spirit ribbon is different from anything I’ve ever seen.” Urahara said, his voice low,
“Not an arrancar or a hollow, not a shinigami or a quincy either. You feel human, yet there is
something else tied to your soul that says otherwise.”
“I don’t know what you’re talking about!” Her voice shook, “What do you want?”
“Just to have a friendly little chat.” Urahara said, flaring his fan once more to cover his face,
“Something strange happened a few days ago. A foreign energy signature leaked into
Karakura Town, one that ripped apart the very fabric of reality. I was curious, and more than
a bit surprised to see two children responsible for it.”
“You…” Oracle flinched back, “You knew we were here this whole time?”
“That’s correct!” A calculated gleam entered his shadowed eyes, “I wanted to see what you
would do, but you two seemed so out of place. It was rather sad to watch. Besides, your
strange reiatsu alerted the Soul Society. I’ve held them off for now, but it’s only a matter of
time before they send a team to capture and interrogate you.”
Capture? Interrogate!?
Soul Society?
Is that where those other strange people were from, wearing shape-shifting swords and black
kimono? What were those other monsters? Coming in all shapes and sizes, their heads always
covered with a bone white mask, their bloodlust stained the air like a thick smog.
Urahara studied her as the silence stretched.
“Well, the information you have wouldn’t be for free!” He tapped the fan against the palm of
his other hand, “I can provide you protection and a place to stay. Maybe, I could even help
you return to wherever you came from.”
“You… could really do that?” She whispered.
He took off his bucket hat and placed it over his heart, “If it’s within my power, little lady.
Plus, I haven’t had anything this interesting to study in years. It can get rather boring after a
century or two of idleness.”
Oracle folded her hands together. Her mask scanned Urahara, readings with body
temperature, his heart rate, and breathing popped up across her vision. Everything was

normal, calm.
“I—”
“Get away from her!!” Skull burst through the door in full costume, electricity snapping at
the air in roiling serpents, “PERSONA, Seiten Taisei!!”
“Skull, wait!” Oracle cried, but it was too late.
Seiten Taisei appeared out of a curtain of blue flames and charged forth on a black cloud,
swinging his bludgeoning staff with the full force of thunderstorm.
Urahara grinned in amusement as he deflected the blow with his fan, sparks flew as if it were
made of steel. Seiten Taisei curled his lips in a snarl and his weapon blurred as he struck
again.
Urahara met the attack head on with nothing more than a fan.
Oracle’s mouth dropped as lightning crackled around the warehouse, winds whipped between
the two figures as their energies clashed, but the winner was clear. Urahara stared in
amusement as the Persona was repelled with a simple flick of his fan.
Seiten Taisei reeled back, slamming into the wall with a loud crash and a plume of smoke.
“For real!?” Skull cried as he placed himself in front of Oracle, “What the hell is this guy!?”
“That was impressive!” Urahara laughed as he dusted himself off, “You almost caught me off
guard. Almost. Not quite, though. It was a good try!”
“I’ll show you impressive, old man!” Skull grinned as Seiten Taisei pulled himself from the
dent in the wall.
“Skull, stop—”
The sunlight was snuffed out as dark clouds converged over the warehouse before lightning
crashed through the rooftop and struck Urahara. Or it would have, if the man didn’t suddenly
vanish.
“Knock it off!” Oracle grabbed Skull’s wrist, “He’s not a threat!”
“That’s bullshit!” Skull whipped around, “You know we can’t trust anyone here,
especially shady adults!”
“M-maybe, but my readings said he wasn’t lying.” Oracle curled her hands into fists, “I’m so
tired. Do you want to keep staying in this stupid warehouse? Do you want to stay cold and
hungry? Do you want to find a way home or do you want to be stuck here forever? What
other choice do we have, Skull!?”
He blinked several times, leaning back from her fury, “But…I…”

“I would listen to her.” They whirled around to Urahara, who appeared behind them, “She
has a good head on her shoulders.”
“Shut up! Seiten Tensei!!”
“I see you like to play with lightning,” Urahara sighed as he pointed to Skull, Seiten Tensei
charged at Urahara with his weapon raised over his head, “But like the little lady, I like to
study my opponents. So I know your weakness.”
Seiten Tensei’s shadow fell over Urahara, but he didn’t move.
Oracle gasped at the spike of power on her HUD from Urahara… which spoke of wind
magic. Skull’s weakness.
“Hadou number 58, Tenran.”
“STOP IT!”
A tornado swirled around the warehouse, throwing up boxes and trash. Seiten Tensei wailed
as the wind hit him, Skull cried out as he was knocked on his backside.
Prometheus wrapped around her and and her quick fingers flew across her holographic
keyboard. The tornado stuttered to a halt, dropping trash and making a general mess of the
warehouse. Glowing alien glyphs surrounded her and Skull, forming a circular barrier around
them.
Prometheus hovered over them, the sunlight splashing them in dramatic light and shadow.
Urahara hummed curiously as he approached the glowing circle, the light cast him in sharp
contrast. He poked the edge of the barrier with his shoe and hissed at the tiny sparks that
nipped at his toes.
“Ha!” Skull, despite his sweaty face, muttered with a manic grin, “Beat that!”
“Skull, enough!” She snapped, Prometheus’ following growl rumbled through the warehouse
with her, “And you!”
Oracle’s screens showed Urahara clutching his chin in thought as he studied her glyphs. He
looked up at her, still amused.
“I thought you wanted to help, but you sit there and shoot a tornado at us?”
The man blinked up at the giant floating orb encased in black fire, eyes still calculating.
“I wanted to see how you would react to the situation.” He playfully waved his fan towards a
scowling Skull mere inches away, “You have pretty fast reflexes, so you do have battle
experience after all. I’m impressed!”
“What the hell is going on in here?”

A woman had suddenly appeared behind Urahara. She was slender, with golden eyes and tan
skin, her hair flowing down her back in a pony tail.
“Kisuke!” She smacked him on the back of his head, “What are you doing? Their reiatsu is
leaking through the barriers like a sieve! Do you want the Seireitei to locate them? Honestly,
they’re just as bad at controlling their reiatsu as Kurosaki!”
“I had it handled, Yoruichi!” He said, though he avoided her eyes like a scolded toddler.
“Right. Handled.” She crossed her arms and pinned him with a stern glare, “’Handled’
would’ve been all of us safe and sound back at the shop by now, not whatever this is. Look
kids, I’ll apologize to you for this idiot, he gets reckless when he gets too excited.”
“Not true.” Urahara waved his fan, but she snatched it out of his grasp and smacked him in
the forehead with it.
“Now, we can keep playing and get caught, or we could all get somewhere safe. Your
choice.”
The woman kept a straight face as Urahara tried and failed to take his fan back, like a kid
reaching for a toy. Prometheus floated back to the ground, where both the circle of glyphs
and the persona dissipated into thin air.
Oracle pointedly looked at Skull. “I’ll apologize for my idiot too—”
“Hey!”
“He can be pretty reckless and stupid, he never thinks these things through.”
Skull sighed, “I’m sittin’ right here, you know.”
“I like you, kiddo.” Yoruichi smiled at Oracle as her eyes glimmered with humor, “You have
a name?”
Oracle closed her eyes, her costume burning away into casual clothes. The adults blinked in
surprise as she pushed up her thick glasses and placed both of her hands behind her back.
“Sakura Futaba, my code name is Oracle.”
“Yoruichi Shihoin. It’s a pleasure meeting you, Sakura-san.”
Futaba nudged Skull with her foot.
He rolled his eyes as his costume disappeared into oblivion, “Whatever. Name’s Sakamato
Ryuji, code name Skull.”
“Why do you have code names?” Urahara asked.
“Kisuke, save the questions for later.” Yoruichi waved for them to follow, “Let’s go.”

“Can I have my fan back?”
“Nope, it’s mine now.” Yoruichi fanned her face with a smirk, “Officially confiscated.”
“You’re so mean!”
“Get over it. You have a whole horde of them back home!”
Futaba smiled at their antics. For some reason, it reminded her of how Ren and Morgana
bantered back and forth, whether it be at Leblanc, Mementos, or within a Palace. The thought
soothed her heart, just a little.
Ryuji grumbled as he finally got to his feet, his distrust was as plain as the scowl on his face.
He hovered in front of her protectively, his eyes never leaving the adults.
Futaba held his hand in both of hers, a reassuring smile spread on her face. His eyes softened
a little, but tension still lined his shoulders. She followed the two strange adults with Ryuji at
her side. They would both feel a little better with a few hours of sleep and some decent food
in their bellies, then they could get to work.
Then they could find a way to rescue the others.

Chapter 19: Restlessness
Chapter Summary

“Villain!”
Bakugo’s eyes were blown wide as he whipped his head towards the stands.

AWESOME FANART!

~*~*~*~

“Stop acting like a disgraceful child!” Endeavor loomed over his son, the heat of his flames
soaking the hallway, “You would’ve blown past the competition if you used your fire!”
“I’ll win without using fire.” Todoroki scowled, “I don’t need your power.”
Endeavor scoffed, “You’ll reach the limits of your mother’s quirk. Did you forget that you’re
different from your siblings? You are my grand masterpiece, you need to cease this childish
tantrum and use your flames!”
“I am not your ‘masterpiece’,” Todoroki walked around his father, face filled with murder, “I
don’t need you to win.”
He stomped down the hallway, mind so muddled with rage that he didn’t notice the little girl
waiting around the corner. Endeavor growled, his swirling flames mirrored the frustrated
whirlpool around his heart.
Alice felt a tug on her soul.
“Alice? What are you doing?” Joker asked.

“Heehee!” Her grin would unsettle the meanest of men, “I wanted to play hide and seek with
Ectoplasm.”
“You promised you wouldn’t play, but I’m glad you did. The distraction saved us in the nick

“I only promised not to play with my teddies, so you’re welcome, big brother. I only need
another second, promise!”
“Alice—”
Alice stepped around the corner and revealed herself.
Endeavor raised a brow, turning fully towards her. His skin itched underneath her gaze, the
hairs were raised on the back of his neck. Something about this child was off, but he
swallowed it down and took a step closer.
“What are you doing here, little one?” He asked, “There shouldn’t be anybody else back
here.”
A sickly purple glow highlighted her body as death and despair seeped into the fabric of
reality, her face split in half with a demonic grin and her eyes began to glow like red hot
coals. Her golden locks wriggled like serpents.
“If you know what’s good for you,” Her sickly sweet giggle turned his blood into ice, “Then
you’ll be nicer to my big brother. This will be your one and only warning.”
Endeavor swore as dread consumed him like a thousand chittering insects. The girl twirled
around and a sudden blinding light drowned out all color. He shielded his eyes as he flung
himself back, but she vanished by the time the stars left his vision. There was only the fading
chill of death as evidence she was ever there. He shivered as he willed his flames to cover
him like a wool blanket.
That little girl’s terrifying laughter would torment him for weeks.

Hitoshi paced the hallway, the roar of the crowd trickled in from the sun draped opening and

Hitoshi took another deep breath to calm his rabbiting heart, his mind wandered to his hero.
What would Joker do? A single video with Joker’s voice revealed his confidence and suave
authority, he held the hero world in his palm and shattered the grimy veil of blind worship.

What he would give to meet Joker, but that was just a pipe dream.

But could he really do that to his parents? He loved the Blue Lotus and respected what his

“Introducing the blazing green star that took first place in the obstacle course and got his

“Sorry Midoriya, but I have to do whatever it takes to be a hero. I have to step up and prove

Only a few more steps until his win, when Midoriya suddenly stopped. Hitoshi’s scalp

Midoriya went on the offensive.

A chunk of that hateful ice melted away into dim hope.
“Thanks, I guess.”
He walked out of the arena, the encouraging calls of his general course classmates put a smile
on his face. That smile fell as he ducked into the hallway and away from the arena. The next

His phone vibrated a few times. He expected his parents to send their encouragements or

“Start!!”

Smoke plumes and dust peppered the air, the constant pops and booms pounded into the

She waited until he launched himself again, floating high in the air like a bird of prey ready

Bakugo would never admit to the tiny smidgen of respect that had bloomed for her.

Besides, he would prove to these damn extras that he wasn’t a villain.

Akira left the stadium despite the fireworks and the cheers rumbling through the grounds. His

Every step closer to the U.A. gate was agonizing. Anything could happen between here and

Akira let their words fade into the background as he glanced back at the golden insignia

Besides, no possible Treasure would ever be safe from the Phantom Thieves.

Chapter End Notes

Hey everyone! Well, that concludes the Sports Festival, I felt that there wasn't really a
need to hash out every canon fight and make it longer than it should be necessary so I
only included the two that I think would be most impactful. I think other BNHA fic
writers will agree that the Sports Festival can be a ROYAL PAIN IN THE REAR to
write and I'm glad I found a way to shorten it.

Chapter 20: Sunset Bridge
Chapter Notes

Edits on 3/18/2023

See the end of the chapter for more notes

Akira added the final touch of cream and sugar and gave it a stir. Curls of steam pleasantly
rose from the cup of coffee as he whisked it to Hitoshi’s table.
“Your coffee, as promised.” Akira said as he set it down.
“Thanks.”
Akira frowned when Hitoshi glared at his open laptop, “If you’re still upset over yesterday
—”
“I’d be a liar if I said I still wasn’t mad over that.” Hitoshi shrugged, “But it’s something else.
I’ve been doing some digging on the Hero Killer since the news compares him so much to
Joker. There are some things that don’t really add up.”
Akira blinked, “Like what?”
“Stain was relatively unknown before Joker took down Silver Falcon.” He sipped his coffee
and scrolled through the web page, “He had a small following, and the news didn’t care about
him.”
“What are you getting at?”
“I just find it odd how Stain gained so much attention all of a sudden.” Hitoshi sighed, “It’s
like somebody used Joker’s sudden fame to fuel Stain’s ideals to a much broader audience.
The sad thing is that it’s working, and now Joker and Stain are nearly synonymous to each
other. There’s always some new article comparing them whenever I check.”
Akira sank into the opposite booth with a frown, “It does sound suspicious.”
“I haven’t found any concrete evidence, so I don’t know if its a coincidence or not.” Hitoshi
shrugged, “That, or the conspiracy theorist in me just doesn’t know when to quit.”
“What do you know about Stain?”
“Where to even begin.” Hitoshi blinked slowly, and took another sip of coffee before he
spoke, “Rumor has it that Stain was a vigilante called Stendhal before he snapped and started
murdering heroes, and walked a pretty bloody path since.”

“How many victims?”
Hitoshi hummed as he typed his laptop, “He’s murdered 17 known pros and permanently
crippled another 22. Well, 23 now. Ingenium got hit in Hosu during the Sports Festival
yesterday, there was an article this morning stating that he might be permanently
handicapped.”
Akira frowned as he looked out the front windows.
Something sour took to the air since Stain’s attack on Ingenium. Was it fear? Uncertainty? It
was in the eyes of everyone he passed this morning, in hushed whispers that spoke of the
merciless brutality. It was similar to the dread that plagued Shibuya during Kaneshiro’s reign,
but Stain’s reach extended all over Japan.
His gut instinct screamed at him to fix this before Stain could maim anyone else.

with something simple before moving on to the more complex recipes.”

A whole week, one day to get Aiba to Gentle Criminal, and then the rest to scour Hosu for

“Okay.”

Akira nodded. Ayumu rolled his eyes, to which she turned to him with a frightening smile.

The moon hung high a city soaked in fear.
Shoto watched his father’s writhing flames part the crowds as they marched through the
streets. He thought his father would teach him about the unwieldy power of flame, not go
hunting the Hero Killer in some single minded obsession.
His father’s scowl deepened as the night dragged on. Villains had gone to ground at word of
Endeavor’s arrival. No sign of Stain, either. They crossed another intersection when Shoto
caught a sliver of movement above. He froze in his tracks.
There, perched on the corner of a building, was Joker.
The moon outlined him in silver, a breeze gently ruffled his long coattails and his unkempt
hair. Joker’s cat curled around his shoulders, glaring. Their startling blue and steely eyes met
his own. Neither of them moved. Each held their breath, but Joker’s red-gloved hand reached
down for the hilt of his dagger.
Joker’s eyes stabbed into him as if he waited for Shoto to alert Endeavor. Shoto’s pounding
heart counted the seconds that ticked by, the outside world faded away until it was the three
of them locked in an eternal staring contest. Shoto slowly relaxed his rigid stature.
Something softened in Joker’s eyes and a cocky smirk broke through, his stiff shoulders
drained of tension.
“Shoto!”
The rest of the world snapped back into place as Shoto whipped his head towards Endeavor,
whose face was twisted in a sneer.

“Don’t fall behind! You have no time for idle distractions.”
He kept a straight face and nodded, only risking a glance when Endeavor turned his back.
Joker vanished from the rooftops like a phantom. Excitement bubbled underneath his stoic
expression as he caught up to his father, but that begged the question.
What was Joker doing in Hosu?

True to her word, the faceless Nomu finally emerged back onto the streets. A few shards of
ice and broken cement clung to it’s skin, but its wounds were regenerating.
“Go.” Joker held his arm out to Gran Torino and Manual, “I’ll distract it while you flee.”
“Ha!” Gran Torino grinned, “As if. I haven’t had excitement like this in years.”
“We’d only slow you down.” Manual and the other heroes formed a protective wall as the
citizens scurried away from danger, “We’re counting on you!”
Joker sighed in relief as they disappeared down the street. USJ Junior gurgled and tore the icy
chunks from it’s flesh, its wounds stitched back together in seconds.
Joker would help the old hero with the last Nomu, as long as they didn’t get recognized. He
flexed the hand with the grappling hook hidden underneath his sleeve, eyes scanned over the
rooftops. It never hurt to have an immediate escape.
“Look out, big brother!!”

A stream of fire shot blasted USJ Junior back into the building. Joker looked over his
shoulder. Endeavor stood at the opposite side of the street, hands smoking. The ice melted
under his feet.
“It’s… it’s him!!” Alice’s power trickled into his mask, “I told him to be nice to my big
brother! I’ll make him pay!”
“Alice, no!” Arsene yanked her back, “Your power is not what the Trickster needs right
now!”
“But…” Alice’s rage was colder than arctic ice, “But I warned him. I want him to suffer!”
“No, little one. Leave him to me!” Cerberus said, “His flame shall not burn me!”
Alice whisked off into the depths of Joker’s mindscape without another word.
Joker smirked as he met eyes with Endeavor, “Cerberus!”
Titania disappeared, Cerberus rose in her place and stepped in front of Joker protectively.
Rage flashed over the hero’s face as he thrust his arm out, a stream of red hot fire reflected
within the icy mirrors.
Gran Torino cursed as he soared to safety, landing next to Endeavor and smacking the man’s
leg with his cane, “What are you doing!?”
“Eliminating a criminal.” Endeavor cut off the stream, “I’ll give you the benefit of the doubt,
esteemed elder, since he manipulated you. That boy is Joker, a vigilante wanted by the Hero
Commission.”
“The one who took down Silver Falcon?” The old man’s eyes flew wide open, he whipped
around to face the unharmed vigilante and his beast, “You really can’t judge a book by its
cover.”
Cerberus yawned as tendrils of steam wafted from him, “Even my flames are hotter than
these embers.”
“You’ll be safer on Cerberus.” Joker whispered to Morgana.
The not-cat grimaced, but hopped from his usual perch. Morgana looked adorable when he
climbed on Cerberus, like a tiny lion cub pestering its parent. Endeavor sneered as Joker
scratched Cerberus behind the ear, then stepped around the beast to give them his best shit
eating grin.
“I was wondering if anybody would recognize me.” Joker gave Endeavor the two finger
salute, “Flameo, hotman!”
Endeavor’s flames fluctuated as his hands curled into fists. Gran Torino held out his cane to
stop him from firing, then glanced over at Joker with narrowed eyes.

“What’s wrong?” Joker splayed his arms out, his devious smirk split his face in two, “Not
going to attack? Why don’t you use your flames again, hero?”
Endeavor’s temper boiled over and the whole street was alight with a righteous blaze. Gran
Torino swore, but it was already too late. Ice melted into puddles, which then evaporated into
steam by the volcanic heat, the vigilante was utterly consumed in the white hot blaze.
Endeavor cut off his attack with a smirk of his own.
Both of the heroes startled when laughter echoed from the pyre. A shape emerged from it, the
boy with glowing sunset eyes and a grin to match his undying gall. He was untouched. There
were no burns despite the cement melting at his feet. Joker looked like the Prince of Hell with
how the fires danced around him and shadowed his glowing eyes.
Color drained from Endeavor’s face, his eyes as wide as dinner plates.
“What’s wrong?” Joker placed his hands on his hips, “Is that all you have, number two?”
“If…if you know what’s good for you kid,” A healthy mix of disbelief and awe came into the
old hero’s eyes, “You would turn yourself in.”
“That sounds fun and all,” Joker bowed like a true showman, “But I have bigger fish to fry.
See ya!”
Joker back flipped onto Cerberus, snowy white fur spilled from between his fingers as he
clung to the persona’s mane. Concrete scraped underneath Cerberus’s claws as he bounded
down the street. USJ Junior emerged from the broken building as they sped by.
“I’ll get the kid, you handle the Nomu.”
“Fine.” Endeavor growled as the old hero shot off.
Endeavor launched himself at USJ Junior, their fists colliding in a brilliant display of power.
Morgana snickered at Gran Torino as he shot towards them like a missile.
“I don’t think so.”
Magical winds knocked the the old man from the air. Joker felt a little twinge as he
plummeted back to the ground, locked in place by a ruthless tornado.
“I’ll keep him there until we get away!” Morgana said, “Hopefully the Nomu keeps Endeavor
busy.”
They left the sounds of battle behind and into deserted streets. Cerberus slowed to a stop
when he deemed it safe enough.
“You were amazing back there.” Joker patted the massive beast’s shoulder, “All of you
were.”
Seth snorted and Titania chuckled. Yatagarasu ruffled his feathers in pride.

“Always happy to serve, Master!!” Cerberus said, his tail wagging, “It was really fun!”
They hopped down from the Persona’s back before becoming nothing more than embers
himself. Joker had eyes for the rooftops. The grappling hook hurled them to the top of the
closest building.
“That battle is bound to get attention.” Morgana said, “Not to mention how many people saw
us fly half way across the city on Seth.”
“The news stations are going to have fun tonight.”
Joker turned to look out into the city. It was…. rather devastating. The night sky was snuffed
out by great pillars of smoke, sirens rang out across the city locked in an aura of panic and
fear. Hot winds disheveled his hair. He dug into his pouches for his phone.
“What are you doing?” Morgana asked.
“I’m sure Aiba will be able to give us the full scope of what’s going on. Maybe she’ll know
where…” Joker furrowed his brow at a new text from Midoriya, sent only minutes ago,
“Why would he send all of his contacts a random location?”
“Hey, weren’t we in that area last night?” Morgana peeked at the screen, “That is here in
Hosu, right?”
“What’s Midoriya doing in Hosu?”
Dread spiked in his heart. The phone was thrown back into his pocket as he took off towards
Midoriya’s location.
Morgana clung onto his shoulder for dear life, “Where are we going!?”
“I have a hunch,” Joker forced his legs to move faster, “I know exactly where Stain is.”
Morgana gaped at him, but he met Joker’s eyes with determination of his own, “Alright then,
let’s do this!”
“We’ll get there faster on Seth.”
“F-fine.” Morgana’s ears went flat against his head. “The faster the better.”
Seth’s excitement redoubled when he was summoned and they took off into the sky, yearning
to taste the blood of his prey.

FAN ART!!

Bloodlust drowned the children, it climbed down their throats and seized their hearts in fear.
Every fibre of their being fought for the next heart beat, the next breath.
Thud.
Ice and fire didn’t stop the serial killer’s jagged blade which sang of the blood spilled and
bones broken with every swing. The wall was no comfort for Midoriya’s fall as he was
paralyzed. He watched in horror as Stain raised his horrible weapon to cleave his friend in
half.
Thud.
“Todoroki!”
“Recipro Burst!!”
The snap of metal echoed as Stain’s sword broke under engine fire. Iida twisted around, his
other leg spewed smoke and flame as he kicked Stain with his full power. Stain was thrown
back in a hail of flowing scarves as he slid to a stop, his expression cut into a dangerous
scowl as the sword dropped with a clatter.
Thud.
“Iida!” Midoriya eyes teared up in relief.
“You can move!” A knot in Todoroki’s chest unfurled, “His quirk isn’t so great after all.”
“Todoroki, Midoriya.” Iida hung his head in shame, “I apologize for getting you mixed up in
this.”

Stain’s eyes glowed with malice. He whipped out a serrated dagger and lunged forward, but
he never managed more than a single step.
THUD.
A massive black shadow fell over the alley, followed by a stormy winds. Todoroki and Iida
shielded their faces against it, but Midoriya and the unresponsive hero were left helpless.
Joker plummeted, golden eyes crinkled from the grin upon his face as he pointed a gun at
Stain mid-air.
Gunshots pierced their eardrums.
Stain backpedaled several steps as one bullet pierced his shoulder. The wind died down as the
vigilante landed as graceful as a dancer, weapons gleaming under the bleeding moon.
“Sorry for the delay, everyone.” Joker stood fully, the smoking gun, “It’s not a real party
unless somebody arrives fashionably late.”
“J-Joker!?” Midoriya’s jaw dropped as relief flooded his eyes, “What are you d-doing here!?”
Iida tensed, “The same vigilante from the USJ…?”
Todoroki’s jaw dropped.
“Joker?” Stain’s eyes narrowed, “You brought down Silver Falcon.”
“Pleased to make your acquaintance, Stain.” Joker twirled his gun around his finger, “You’re
just the man I’ve been looking for.”
Stain lowered his serrated dagger, “Why are you looking for me?”
Joker retrieved a red and black card from his breast pocket, which the vigilante held between
his pointer and middle finger. With a flick of his wrist, he sent the card hurling at Stain like a
throwing knife. Stain caught it, eyes scanning over the words.
“What is this drivel?” Stain’s lips curled as he crushed it with his fist.
“It’s your calling card, Stain.” Joker widened his stance and pointed his gun at Stain, “It’s
your personal invitation from me to put a stop to your slaughter. You should be honored.”
“Stop me? I thought you would be one to understand my creed.” Stain tossed the card aside,
“You’re just like the rest of these fake heroes!”
Joker scoffed, “Tell me Stain, why do you choose to kill ‘fake heroes’?”
“Because it’s the only way!” Stain jabbed his dagger towards Iida, “False heroes plague this
society, they are a disease that must be cleansed. Only true heroes like All Might deserve the

“I’ve proven you don’t need to kill them. Silver Falcon will be in prison for a long time.”

“A man like Silver Falcon will be stuck in his ways for the rest of his life.” Stain sneered,
“Don’t tell me that you’re so blind. That ‘hero’ should’ve been purged properly.”
“I agree people can’t change if they don’t want to,” Joker’s smirk fell, his eyes turned

Might. That’s an impossible standard, given that he’s the number one hero.”
Midoriya’s fingers twitched in the corner of his eye. Good, he just needed to keep Stain

of a nearby rooftop, watching his back.
“I see words won’t get through to you,” Stain growled as he shifted on his feet, “Die like the

Stain leapt, blade held high over his head. Another smirk split Joker’s face as Seth roared

Joker looked over his shoulder to Todoroki, his left side steaming. They met eyes once again,

“Don’t face him alone.” Todoroki stopped beside Joker, flames licked at his left side, “He’s

“I know, Peppermint,” Joker chuckled, “Can you use those those flames of yours to keep him

“Peppermint…?” Todoroki muttered quietly, then he shook his head, “You can leave it to
me.”
“Todoroki,” Iida stared at his friend in shock, “You’re trusting a vigilante?”
“What choice do we have?” He kept his glare on Stain, “I don’t think we can handle a three

“Todoroki…” Midoriya glanced over to Joker, “Iida, he’s right. Joker’s on our side!”
“But he’s a criminal! I…” Iida scowled and curled his hands into fists.
“Criminal or not, you’re injured.” Joker held his arm out, “Let me handle him from here.”
Iida’s eyes went to the ground, but he said nothing.
“Trickster! The alleyway is too narrow for me!” Another tempest beat them down as Seth

“Follow through with Plan C,” Joker’s smirk grew, “We’ll flush him out into the street.”

“Roger!!”

“What!? What kind of plot are you hatching!?” Iida shouted.

A great shadow hovered ominously at the mouth of the alley, Seth’s pure golden eyes were
trained in on the serial killer.
He opened his great maw and bellowed a war cry, shaking the very foundations around them.
Joker chuckled as the others covered their ears and dust rained down from above, garbage
cans and dumpsters toppled over. They were whipped by a whirlwind as Seth flapped his

“Stand back and wait for my signal.”
Midoriya furrowed his brow, “What do you—”
Joker charged, brandishing his pistol and dagger. Stain’s manic grin matched the masked

A sudden surge of killing intent suffocated Joker, the mere moment it took to recover cost

“Joker!!”
Todoroki and Midoriya’s voices shouted in unison as Stain ran his rugged blade down Joker’s

Joker recovered and flowed into a roundhouse kick, the blow knocking his opponent back.
He could feel the U.A. kids’ horror melt into relief when not a single drop of blood was shed.
Stain glowered at his clean daggers before he looked back at Joker. His grin showed too
many teeth.
“You have some impressive friends, Ingenium!!” Stain howled with mad laughter as he

Ingenium?
Joker filed that information away for later as he ducked underneath a deadly swipe. Todoroki

Desperation lined Stain’s movements as he threw himself to the side, Iida’s engines roared

“I thought I told you to stay back, Motorboat!” Joker teased.

Joker threw his head back and laughed, “Isn’t it a bit too late for your pity party?”
Iida’s jet fueled leg flew through the air, Stain sneered and lifted his dagger to counter him.

“Enough!”
Stain panted and hauled himself to his feet, he dug something out of his pouches. Joker

It was a Life Stone.
Stain crushed it in his hand and they watched in horror as his injuries healed.
Joker scowled and charged with his dagger at the ready when three flashes of steel sliced

Joker snapped his fingers, a hidden signal.
The knives were batted away by a gust of wind and clattered uselessly against the wall. Iida

“What was that!?” Midoriya shouted.
Joker aimed his gun at Stain, silent, but then Seth hit the zenith. He felt an unimaginable

“Fall back!” Joker shouted, “Get out of the alleyway!”
Todoroki threw up a jagged spire of ice at the Hero Killer to slow him down, then threw

There was a whistle to the air, almost like a bomb dropping.

Joker stood in front of the other kids as they huddled around the corner. Seth waited until the

The alleyway exploded into a maelstrom that ripped through stone and ice alike, Stain was no

“Todoroki, I can move now.”

“No.” Joker grimaced, “He’s not done yet.”
Midoriya inhaled sharply as Stain, bloodied and bruised, scraped himself off of the concrete.
Crimson streaked the Hero Killer’s body, a terrifying smile split his face and his eyes were

“He’s mine!”
A dragon’s cry made the night air tremble, and Seth jumped from the rooftops. His claws dug

There was a sickening smack as Stain flew through the air for a second time.
Joker wouldn’t waste this opportunity.
The role of Leader fell onto his shoulders so naturally, the faces of the U.A. teens blurred into
that of his friends.
“Now!” Joker was the first to move, “Surround him and do an all out attack!”
They briefly exchanged glances, but scrambled to follow before the Hero Killer could

Wild green electricity ran over Midoriya’s body like serpents, the concrete cracked

Joker heard the crack of ribs as the two fell back, but Joker surged onward, his dagger leaving

The Hero Killer didn’t move.

“He’s…” Midoriya swallowed, “He’s finally down…”
Joker sheathed his weapons and tugged on his blood red gloves, “This show’s finally over.”
“You!!”
Joker dropped as Iida’s leg soared over his head, the roar of engines screamed in Joker’s ears

“Iida, stop!” Todoroki shouted, but it was futile.
Midoriya waved his hands, “Wh-what are you doing!?”
“Stain is captured, now it’s his turn!”
“Oh, so that’s how it is, Ingenium?” Joker teased with a limber back flip, “I’m glad you still

“Shut up!” Iida’s eyes darkened into something dangerous, “How dare you mock the name of
Ingenium!!”
Seth howled his fury, the earth shook as he hurled himself at Iida, jaws wide open.
The mirth was wiped from Joker’s face, “Seth, no!”
The dragon had no choice but to obey, whipping his tail to change his momentum. Seth

Todoroki was torn between his hero and his friend.
Midoriya wrung his hands together, mind whirring to find a peaceful solution.
Joker’s infuriating grin slithered back onto his face. He might’ve saved them from Stain’s

Joker slowly tilted his head to the side, “Because you’re going to let me go.”

Iida’s rage fell into shock, “As if! Why would I would release you after everything you’ve

Todoroki’s expression was a stoic mask, but there were lingering emotions in his eyes that

“You’ve also felt like this? Did…” Iida swallowed, his eyes desperately searching Joker’s

Midoriya paled.
Todoroki’s eyes became somber.

Seth towered over Midoriya as his throat lit up with a Maragidyne, the flames leaked from

Seth snapped his jaws shut, the fire in his throat was extinguished and curls of smoke escaped

No, it was something much worse than that.
“Trickster, this hero…” Arsene whispered.
“I know.”

“Are you going to heal Native, too?” Midoriya whispered, “Is he—”

“I sense no other Metaverse items on Shitstain,” Seth said to fill the dreaded silence.

“What do you plan to do?” Arsene said.
“Perhaps we do nothing, leave him for the other heroes.” Yatagarasu suggested.
“And what?” Titania crossed her arms, “What if they blame the Trickster for his death?”
“Why blame the Trickster when Stain is the obvious answer?” Yatagarasu said, “It wouldn’t

“Can we really take a chance like that?”
“We can surpass death.”
Joker shivered at this persona’s voice.
“You!” Titania snapped, “Can’t you just be quiet!?”
“Silence! Let the Trickster think on it.”
The hero hasn’t been dead for more than ten minutes.
What was the risk? What was the reward? The hero wouldn’t remember dying, would he?
Joker rolled the various outcomes around in his mind. At the same time, there may not be
another chance to test this spell.
Aside from breaking into a morgue.
He might be a thief, but even he had standards.

“Big brother,” Alice whispered, “We can break the cycle of life and Death. Our powers are
unmatched in this world.”
“Are you saying that as the ultimate persona of Death?” Arsene asked.
“...I am.”
Joker sighed,“Let’s give it a shot.”
Seth faded away as silent as a breeze.
Joker donned another Persona as his mask, but did not let them manifest before casting
Samarecarm. Glowing flowers sprouted over the concrete, bringing the fresh breath of life on

Joker’s jaw dropped as the butterfly melded into the man’s skin and he jolted to life with

He felt eyes on him, and he turned to see the three U.A. kids staring at him, highlighted by

Joker nodded, and Midoriya’s relieved smile was akin to sunshine. Iida put a hand to his heart

Then, like a ghost, he slipped into the nearby alley when the unmistakable glow of Endeavors

“What about Shitstain?”
“Leave him for the heroes.”
“Bah!” Seth snorted, “Shitstain wasn’t even a challenge, more of a one trick pony. What a
disappointing hunt.”
Joker snorted as he stepped over icy shards, “I’ll make it up to you somehow.”
“Hmph. Only a fight to the death will satisfy me! That shall be my reward, Trickster.”
“I’ll… keep that in mind.”
“Flying upon my great form would only draw unwanted attention,” Seth’s grumbled, “We
must make haste, like a rabbit fleeing the fox’s jaws.”
Joker stopped when a crinkle came from his boots.

“Huh, how did you escape Seth’s wrath?” He whispered to himself as he picked up the
crumpled card.
With a shrug, he deposited it back into his pocket. It would make for a nice souvenir, at least.
Joker shot out his grapple, the ride up to the rooftops was nowhere near as exhilarating as

Morgana smirked as he cast magic mid-air, the wind launching him straight towards his
partner like a rocket. Joker almost toppled over when Morgana’s tiny body crashed into his
chest.
“What was that for?” He asked as he cradled the not-cat.
“I was worried!” Morgana narrowed his eyes, tail flicked back and forth.
“Why were you worried? You were backing me up.” Despite himself, he let his best grin
shine, “Don’t tell me you doubted my abilities, Mona.”
“O-of course not!” Morgana climbed from Joker’s arms to his shoulders, “I wasn’t worried
about Stain, he went down easily thanks to the help of those other kids.”
Joker raised a brow, “Then?”
“Fine.” Morgana sighed and rubbed into Joker’s hair, “I was worried about what the U.A.
kids would do to you after, but it seems like my fears were unfounded. Besides, I would’ve
intervened anyway if that blue haired kid didn’t let you go.”
Joker nodded, then turned to look to the streets. He fell into a crouch when Endeavor, Gran
Torino, and a small group of heroes approached Midoriya and the others.
“We should leave before they spot us.” Morgana whispered.
Joker’s eyes narrowed, “I want to make sure that Stain will be properly taken care of first.”
Joker sighed in relief when the heroes took the serial killer and turned on his heel to sneak

“Midoriya!!”
They whipped around just as the winged Nomu soared over the rooftops, with Midoriya in
it’s clutches. Joker whipped out his pistol.
“Shit, Seth—!”
The Nomu lurched as if it were struck with an invisible force, then it fell. A shadow zoomed
past before the Persona materialized, the moonlit form of Stain stabbed the Nomu in it’s
exposed brain and rode the beast into a crash landing. Midoriya was under his arm, paralyzed

by fear as the Hero Killer set him down on the pavement. Seth was held back in the
mindscape, thrashing and stomping, but his master did not let him into the physical plane.
He aimed his pistol as Stain ripped the blade out of the Nomu’s brain.
“Joker…” Morgana’s fur stood on end as the air vibrated with pure malice, “I don’t like
this…”
“What are you standing around for!?” Endeavor stomped down the road, his flames roared.
“Endeavor.” Stain’s mask fell, revealing his gruesome face without a nose, “You fake…”
Goosebumps broke out on Joker’s arms as the bloodlust choked the air and dyed the silver

“Come and get me, you fakes!” Stain stumbled forward a step, “The only one I’ll let kill me
is the true hero, All Might!!”
The evil aura vanished as soon as it came. Stain dropped his bloody knife.
“He’s….” Morgana shivered, “I think he’s unconscious.”
Midoriya was uninjured.
Joker lowered his gun and crept away into the shadows when the heroes captured Stain, for
good this time.
Morgana stayed silent until Joker slowed to a stop halfway across the city. Smoke billowed
from buildings, the wail of sirens and distant shouts echoed through the streets. The turbulent
night was finally coming to an end.
“What a mess,” Morgana said, “It’ll take some time for things to return to normal.”
Joker held out his arm as he summoned Yatagarasu, the faithful bird ruffled his feathers as he
awaited his orders. Morgana blinked curiously as Joker dug out his phone with his other hand
and flicked through his contact list. He scrolled past Taneo’s number. That man would be
getting a call soon, whether he wanted it or not.
“What are you doing?”
“That hero was dead.” Morgana inhaled sharply, but Joker continued as his thumb hovered
over the screen, “Samarecarm actually revived him, so I want to test the strength of other

“Joker,” Morgana was suddenly serious, “We absolutely can’t let it get out that we revived a

“I put him to sleep and cast Makajama on him for good measure. I doubt he’ll remember
what happened tonight at all.”

“Good thinking. So, what were you thinking with these other spells?”
“I’m going to heal Ingenium.”
A beat of silence.
“And if it doesn’t work?”
“We’ll cross that bridge when we come to it, but I think it’ll work. If Samarecarm can revive
the dead, then what can’t our most powerful healing spell fix?”
“If it does work… ” Morgana hummed in thought, “Ingenium was a victim to the Hero
Killer…”
“Yeah, and?”
“Instead of just healing one victim, why don’t we heal them all? It’ll definitely send the

The other heroes will probably try to cover up our involvement in any way possible, but if we

“We’ll sweep them off their feet before they can get a chance to recover! I’ll set something

“Now there’s the Mona I know and love. I’m glad Stain’s little performance didn’t turn you
into a scaredy cat.”
“H-hey! I wasn’t scared before! Not at all!!”
“Of course not.” Joker looked to Yatagarasu, who had watched the entire exchange with
thinly disguised amusement, “Make sure no heroes will get the drop on us.”
Yatagarasu leapt from his arm and soared into the sky. Joker watched the graceful persona for
a moment, then pressed the one and only speed dial. It rang once.
“YOU IDIOTS!!”
Joker held the phone away from his ear as there was a clatter of dishes.
“Manami, please calm down!” Gentle Criminal’s voice filtered through the background,
“You almost spilled the tea.”
“Oh! Sorry, Gentle!”
“Well, I’m glad to hear you guys getting along.”
“You!” Aiba’s wrath returned in full force, “Do you have any idea how worried sick I’ve
been!? Hosu has been all over the news! There are already several videos all over the
internet, and don’t think I didn’t recognize you! You guys promised me that you would be
careful!”

“New videos are up already?” Joker teased, “At least it isn’t a slow news day.”
“Can’t you take this seriously!?”
“Alright, fine. Tell me about these videos.”
“W-well…” He heard the iconic keys typing, “There are several with a dragon flying down

captured you ordering it to attack those monsters. It only shows your back though, so your
face hasn’t been shown.”
“Is that all?”
“No! The media only aired a few videos once since they don’t know who you really are, but
they did call you a ‘mysterious new hero’. There is simply too much information about the
Hosu attack for them to linger on it.” Joker burst out laughing, and Aiba sputtered, “Stop
laughing! This isn’t funny!”
“Of course it is! If only they could knew the irony of this ‘mysterious new hero.’” Joker’s
grin smoothed over, “Anyway, I called to ask for a favor.”
“Fine! Just tell me that you two are okay first? No injuries, right?”
“Yeah, we’re fine. Not even a scratch.”
“Good, that’s… good.” Aiba was silent, he could tell she was still fuming. She sighed in
defeat after a few moments. “Alright, what is it?”
“I need to know where all of the victims for the Hero Killer are located, the ones that are still
alive at least.”
“Why..?”
“I made a promise to somebody and I plan to keep it.”
“You’re not going to do anything stupid, right?”
“Me?” He placed a hand over his heart in mock injury, even though she couldn’t see, “Never.
I’m simply doing them a favor.”
Another sigh came over the line, “It should only take me an hour to get the information. Two
at the most.”
“Thanks, I owe you one.”
“I demand a plate of curry as recompense!” Aiba said, “Don’t ever make me worry like that
again, okay? I don’t know what I would do if I lost my boys.”
She hung up.

“Your boys…?”
Joker stared at his phone for several seconds.
“I heard all of it.” Morgana said, “We have lots of things to do and not much time to do
them.”
“Yup.” Joker pocketed his phone with a sigh, “Lets try to get back to the hideout and rest
before she gets the information.”
“Agreed.”
With that, they disappeared into the smoldering city.

Chapter 23: Butterfly Kisses
Chapter Notes

Edits on 3/21/2023

See the end of the chapter for more notes

Anyone might mistake Iida Tensei for a corpse for how still he was on the hospital bed, death
only kept at bay from the beeping machines around him. The oxygen mask dug into the skin
on his face, but he didn’t have the energy to adjust it. The constant flow of pain meds made
him feel too floaty to sleep despite the lights being turned off and it being dark outside.
He simmered in misery until a soft breeze kissed his face.
It whisked away the horrors whispering in his mind, of his mother’s cries and baby brother’s
heartbroken expression. A presence lingered at his bedside, but there had been no footsteps.
He forced his bleary eyes open at the soft crinkle of paper.
It took him a moment to comprehend the beautiful horned goddess floating serenely, her long
golden hair weaving in moonlight as if she were underwater. Her hand, as delicate as a
freshly bloomed lily, placed a card on the bedside table. The goddess’ expression of calm
tranquility soothed his soul and would make any painter weep
She opened eyes like liquid aquamarines and spoke in a voice of velvet. “Take heart, Iida
Tensei. The Trickster has found you worthy of Salvation.”
The goddess floated over him until her body was parallel with his own. She cupped his face
and placed a gentle kiss on his forehead. He gasped as an ice cold torrent ripped through his
body like a typhoon, but…
It didn’t hurt.
The energy fizzled away his pain and cleared the haze of drugs from his mind, and he felt the
snap as the energy flowed down and out his legs.
The goddess smiled as she floated away, her touch tracing his face before it was gone.
“W-wait!” He shot up, pulling on numerous wires, “What’s your name?”
She bowed and disappeared into a cloud of fluttering cinders.
He sat there, stupefied. With shaky hands he reached for the red and black card with the
insignia of a flaming top hat and mask.

“Take your heart?” Tensei flipped the card over, “To the heroes whose livelihoods were
unjustly taken by the King Of Wrath, who’s reign of bloodshed has been put to an end, we
return what was reaped. Beware, what was given can easily be taken away again. Use this gift
wisely. From, the Leader of the Phantom Thieves of Hearts - Joker?”
Tensei looked to the sticky note on the bottom.
‘Tell your brother I said hi. :)’
…What did this mean?
He stared at his legs, which weren’t numb anymore. His vision blurred when he could move
his toes with no pain. He removed the oxygen mask and various other wires attached to him,
then tore off the blanket. His tears fell freely as he swung his legs over the side and stood to
his full height, the machines’ shrill cries were deafened on his ears as he walked across the
room.
He reread the card again with gentle sobs.
The doors burst open and a medical team rushed in, but they froze when they saw him,
standing, in front of the open window.
“Iida-san!?” The doctor gaped at him like fish out of water, “What… how…. how is this
possible?”
Tensei looked up from the card as more tears fell, “I was kissed by a goddess.”

Three U.A. students sat on the edge of their hospital beds, plunged into their own thoughts.
They were kept overnight for observation despite being uninjured, but none of them had been
able to sleep.
The morose atmosphere was broken by the first spoken words of the day.
“Do you think…”
Todoroki and Midoriya looked to Iida, who hung his head, his hands were tight fists on his

“We would’ve won without Joker?” Iida’s shoulders shook, “If it wasn’t for me and my blind

“It’s hard saying.” Todoroki said after a moment of thought, “Stain was getting desperate
when it was just the three of us. If we were somehow all unaffected by his quirk, then we
might’ve been able to take him down ourselves.”

Midoriya clutched his chin, “How did Joker know where we were in the first place?”
“I have a feeling he was in Hosu because of Stain.”
“Why do you say that, Todoroki?” Iida asked with furrowed brows.
“I saw him on the rooftops the night before the attack.” Todoroki was content to study the

They were interrupted when the door opened. They stood from their beds when a canine
headed man walked in with Gran Torino, Manual, and Detective Tsukauchi.
“Hmph, so you brats are awake.” Gran Torino grumbled.
“G-gran Torino!” Midoriya sputtered.
Iida’s eyes shown with guilt, “Manual…”

The Police Chief towered over everyone else in the room, “As Gran Torino said, I am the

Killer, woof?”
Todoroki narrowed his eyes, “We are.”
“The Hero Killer had fairly serious injuries.” Tsuragamae studied the teens, “Broken bones,
significant bruising, burns, even a few slash wounds to the shoulders. There were traces of a
bullet wound, but it seems to have recently healed over, so that can’t be counted towards
you.”
“What about Native, sir?” Midoriya asked.
Todoroki’s hands balled into fists to hide his shaking.
“He’s awake, but groggy and disoriented.” Tsuragamae cocked his head to the side, “He
doesn’t remember what happened within the last 36 hours, but he should make a full
recovery.”
Iida wasn’t the only one to sigh in relief, but Todoroki remained silent. Tsuragamae’s eyes

“With that aside, the three of you should already know how the laws treat the use of quirks.”
Tsuragamae’s expression became grave, “Even against the Hero Killer, the use of your quirks
without express permission from your guardians is a violation of the law. As such, the three

Todoroki bristled, “You can’t be serious!”

“T-Todoroki!” Midoriya stared at his friend in shock.
“If Iida hadn’t been there, then Native would’ve been killed.” Todoroki stepped around
Midoriya’s bed with an icy cold glare, “If Midoriya and I wouldn’t have come, then Iida

Todoroki trailed off. The room went silent. Tsuragamae cleared his throat after a few

“Do you wish to finish that train of thought, woof?”

“Iida!” Todoroki snapped his head towards his friend.
Tsuragamae and Tsukauchi exchanged significant looks, and Gran Torino grumbled to

“So, the reports are correct.” Tsuragamae ran a hand over his snout, “The notorious vigilante

“What do you mean, sir?” Midoriya said with furrowed brows.
Tsuragamae glanced at Tsukauchi, who nodded.
“I figured you wouldn’t know yet, being cooped up in a hospital room,” Tsukauchi said as he

“It was awe inspiring.” Manual spoke for the first time, “He possessed incredible power with

“That’s an understatement,” Gran Torino said with a scowl, “He took the full brunt of

“He what?” Todoroki asked with wide eyes.
“Come to think of it,” Manual said, “I believe he said the names of those monsters he

Tsukauchi turned to him, pen at the ready, “Do you remember what they were?”
“I believe the dragon’s name was Seth,” Manual frowned, “Then the winged woman was

“What’s wrong, Midoriya?” Iida asked.

“Seth would be an Egyptian god. The god of storms, deserts, and chaos to be more precise.”

Their eyes turned to Iida, who had his hand clasped around his shoulder.

“W-well” Midoriya tapped his chin, “Ribbons of light appeared around us when we were

That Native was dead, until he wasn’t.
Because of Joker.
Thinking about it made his scalp prickle. It kept up him up all night, flitting together with

“Isn’t it a hero’s job to save people? I would’ve done the exact same thing again and again, I

“So? Which would you prefer?” Tsuragamae asked as he lowered his hand, “I personally

“Either way,” Manual smiled and put his hands on his hips, “We’ll need to take responsibility

Tsuragamae looked expectantly at the other two. Midoriya was the first to bow, Todoroki

A knock on the door silenced them all. Tsuragamae nodded towards Manual, who went to

The Chief of Police stiffened, his jaw went slack as he blinked several times. He collected

Iida’s heart hammered in his chest as Tsuragamae handed the paper to Tsukauchi, then looked

Our latest intelligence tells that he has just managed to heal the final hero despite our best

Midoriya and Todoroki’s jaws dropped. Tsukauchi, Gran Torino, and Manual looked at the

Iida began the tale with a shaky voice, he avoided Manual’s eyes until Midoriya added to the

Todoroki looked Tsukauchi right in the eye when he told of Joker’s ‘escape’ and omitted the

In the end, Tsukauchi didn’t pick up any lies.

~*~*~*~

“Shigaraki Tomura, please sit down,” Kurogiri said, “You might reopen your wound.”

“The Hero Killer is still being associated with us because of that new video.”
“That’s not enough!” Shigaraki hissed, “They barely glossed over it!”
Kurogiri silently sighed, the action came off as nothing more than wavering mist. Thankfully,

Shigaraki glowered, “What do you want? I’m not in the mood.”
“Now, is that any way to greet someone who comes bearing gifts?”
Giran placed a few odd stones on the bar, two were perfectly round pearls while the others
were jagged and rough.
“What the hell are these supposed to be?”
“Patience, Shigaraki Tomura.” Kurogiri ignored Shigaraki’s glare as he turned to Giran, “I
didn’t think you would be one to deal in petty drugs, Giran.”
“These are better than any drugs you’d find on the market, and no side effects or addictive
properties to boot.” Giran held out a jagged stone, “They’re healing items. Why don’t you try
one for that shoulder of yours, Shigaraki? You just break it in between your fingers.”
“Quirk enhanced items?” Kurogiri mused as he watched his charge.
Shigaraki’s eyes widened when he broke the stone and cool light washed over his body. The
burn of his shoulder wound lessened, but it was still tender and twinged with pain if he
moved too fast.
“Where did you get these?” Kurogiri asked with growing interest.

“A little bird recently sold them to me, they didn’t share how they got the goods.” Giran
shrugged, “I’m going to try and get more out of them before I share their name. Also, the two
smooth ones are a full heal. I thought your boss would be… interested. I expect my usual
price to be payed, with a little bit of interest.”
Shigaraki scoffed, “Gifts don’t come with a price, Giran.”
“I gave one to the Hero Killer as a sign of good faith, but we all know how that turned out.”
Kurogiri nodded, the rest of the stones were consumed by purple mist before they
disappeared.
“Your accounts will be filled later.”
Shigaraki sank into a bar stool.
“I’ll keep you updated on this special source.” Giran turned for the door, “I’ll also be
bringing you some new recruits, expect them within the next few days.”
“Giran.” The man looked over his shoulder to Shigaraki, “I like you a lot better when you
don’t stink like an ashtray.”
Giran chuckled as he left the bar.

“The analysis is complete, sir.”
“And?”
“W-well, this isn’t a simple item enhanced by a quirk, you see. I didn’t detect any signs of

The wound Shigaraki received from Stain seems to have been mostly healed. If there’s any

All For One reached over and pinched a rough stone, a simple flex from one of his quirks
reduced it to dust. The doctor bit his lip as he watched his master for any sign of change.

There was nothing more than a mild buzzing in his fingertips.
“Hmm, it didn’t work. How disappointing.”

All For One felt the smooth little pearl in his palm. He activated one sensory quirk, then

static.
Interesting.
Without hesitation, he crushed it between his fingers. His skin pleasantly buzzed like a limb
recovering from falling asleep. The doctor fiddled with the mountain of machinery around
All For One.
“Any difference?”
The doctor hummed, “If I didn’t monitor these machines constantly, I would say nothing

They’ve made miraculous claims that all of Stain’s victims have been completely healed, but
the culprit behind these actions leave the hero world baffled.”
The image changed a card with letters cut out from a magazine.
“Joker, the vigilante behind Silver Falcon’s fall from grace, has left calling cards with each
hero. Police have scoured the surrounding areas, but have been unsuccessful in his recapture.
We now go live to a press conference currently being held outside of Hosu General
Hospital.”

The doctor’s eyes flicked to another screen, where Shigaraki began dusting everything in his
reach, rage rolled off of the boy in waves. Kurogiri, with sagged shoulders, released a sigh as

The scene shifted to a sea of reporters crowded in front of the hospital, the Chief of Police

“How did he sneak past security to reach the heroes’ rooms!?” One man shouted, “This

The reporters went wild, blinding camera flashes and countless microphones were shoved

All For One chuckled as he muted the screen.
“S-sir, this is….” The doctor swallowed, the first sparks of insanity lit up his eyes, “If we can

“Yes, it’s possible that his powers could bring me back to my prime.”

All For One’s chuckle echoed within the dark room, “Look.”
He turned his head towards the screens, even though he was blind. Shigaraki was still

“The heroes don’t know how to handle someone as uncontrollable as Joker, the media will

“I understand.”
All For One leaned back in his chair, as content as a king on his throne, “Then we have our
work cut out for us.”
“Y-yes, sir!!”

Hitoshi had been blindsided when he woke up.
The news stations exploded with the healed heroes. Radio hosts and news casters alike
debated on this topic, their voices growing ever more fervent as the morning dragged on.
He scrolled through the endless feed on his laptop, the taste of his mother’s coffee fresh on
his tongue. Hitoshi set the cup down with a frown. He still loved his mother’s coffee, but it
had nothing on Akira’s nectar of the gods. The cafe seemed emptier without Akira for some
reason. He was a new addition, and yet he it was as if he were always meant to be here.
A new message pinged on his Herocord server. It was from a user he often debated with, one
of many that had joined the server to talk about any number of heroes and vigilantes alike.
Joker was the main topic more recently, though.

Hitoshi zoomed in, then flinched back as if he were struck.
A three-legged raven with magatama.
His face drained of color. No, Akira was off helping a friend in a town that wasn’t Hosu, that
hadn’t been on fire or under attack from Stain and Nomu. But the news had mentioned
Joker’s summoning quirk and healing abilities…
Hitoshi rubbed his stomach.
“You can thank the raven for that. And no, before you ask, he’s his own entity. I really am
quirkless.”
The monster with black wings and a top hat, the dragon, a healing demon, and now the raven.
Was Akira lying? No, Hitoshi’s instincts told him that Akira told the truth when he said he
was quirkless. Was really possible for the demons to be their own entity?
“Geez, would it kill you to make any noise when you walk? You remind me too much of my

“Actually, in some circumstances, yes.”

there. The movement itself was in an odd shape, almost as if they were flowing pieces of
fabric.
Or the end of coat tails…
His breathing grew ragged as he rewatched all of the videos with the dragon. There he was
again, commanding the dragon to attack the Nomu.
Hitoshi slammed his laptop closed, eyes wide and palms sweaty.
“What would you say to Joker if he were standing right in front of you?”

He remembered how Akira seemed hesitant to ask, how he looked shocked when Hitoshi
gave him an honest answer. He thought nothing of it at the time.
“Why are you so interested in Stain?” Hitoshi remembered asking.
“I just want to stay informed in case there’s anything new,” Akira had a smile that screamed
of innocent curiosity, “Better than being completely ignorant, right?”
It didn’t make any sense when apart, but if he lined up all of the pieces, then...
His heart hammered out of his chest and he clutched the desk to ground himself from the
sudden dizziness.
The ‘mystery hero’ was Joker.
Akira was Joker.

Taneo jumped when the editor-in-chief slammed her hands on her desk. Her eyes shone with
such zealous hunger that it was as if they were under the scrutiny of an angry goddess.
“You’re telling me nobody has any ideas?” She tucked loose strands of hair behind her ear,

Taneo glanced over to his two coworkers.
Minato Haruka, was a round man with thick glasses, his dark hair was pulled back into a
ponytail. The other, Yuma Takashi, was the youngest in the group, he sported spiked up hair
and baggy clothes.
“Other stations already covered everything.” Minato said, “There hasn’t been any new
information on Joker since the press conference in Hosu. Maybe we can break down the
message on Joker’s calling card?”
“Already been done a dozen times over.” She said, “We need something new.”
Taneo drummed his fingers as he stared at his phone, the darkened screen reflected his
mismatched pupils. If his gut instincts were correct, then it would only be a matter of time
before he called.
“And we can’t just write random bs either,” Yuma leaned back on his seat, “Unless you want

“You’re right.” She got up from her desk and paced the room, “I know! How about we do an

we could do a poll and have our readers vote which ideals they’d want to follow!”

it up to his ear.
“H-hello?”
“Greetings once again, Taneo.”

“I take it you’ve been expecting my call?”
“To put it bluntly, yeah. What do you need?”

“T-Taneo, are you okay?” Minato said with wide eyes, “You’re scaring me.”
“And you’re awfully pale, dude.” Yuma said.
Taneo placed his phone on his desk, then leaned forward with steepled fingers.
His boss placed her hands on her hips, her expression as unreadable as a boulder, “Who was
that?”
“That,” Taneo’s grin turned into a smirk, “Is our ticket to greatness. My best source just
called with a juicy offer. I don’t think I can refuse.”
“About Joker?” She asked, to which he nodded, “Hmm, then I would call them a liar. Joker’s
gone to ground ever since he healed those heroes.”

“And what if I told you that this source were Joker himself?”
Tension and shock stifled the air so much that he could cut it with a knife, perhaps serve it
alongside some cheese and wine. He’ll definitely need a drink after this.
“You’re kidding.”
“Nope. Where do you think I got the video that ended Silver Falcon’s career?”
“That was you!?” His boss lunged at him with a manic look in her eyes, “Then you have to
say yes!! No wait, a regular article just won’t do! A live radio interview, on the other hand…”
“W-wait a second!” Minato stood from his chair, “Wouldn’t that be illegal?”
“Nothing our lawyers can’t get us out of if it goes south. Do you remember when we

“Y-yeah, but because of us the leaders of the kidnapping ring got away, and the yakuza boss

“Details, details!” She waved her hands, “I’ll call in a few favors to secure us a studio!”
“Now, wait a minute.” Taneo held his hands up, “Why don’t we talk everything out with him
first? We might scare him off if he thinks we’re setting up a trap. He has powerful allies who

“And waste this one chance to talk with him? It would be foolish.” She clapped her hands
together, her eyes full of stars, “Well, what are you waiting for!? Call him back this instant!”
Taneo huffed in amusement as he picked up his phone and dialed.

Chapter 24: Wake Up, Get Up, Get Out There
Chapter Summary

The voices reverberated in a double echo, Joker and his interviewer were just past this
door.

Chapter Notes

Edits on 4/16/2023

See the end of the chapter for more notes

The studio was a tiny building right under U.A.’s shadow.
Yatagarasu had watched it for the last several hours to make sure it was safe. Morgana
patrolled nearby and Aiba would do what she always did best with her hacking. His personas,
Arsene in particular, buzzed with excitement as Taneo opened a side door and stepped out
into the alley.
“Let the show begin.” Arsene whispered.
Taneo jumped as Joker landed at the mouth of the alley. The street lights behind him
obscured his face and stretched his shadow over the alleyway.
Taneo put a hand to his heart, “You know how to scare the bejeezus out of someone.”
Joker walked over with practiced confidence, a plastered grin on his face, “It’s nice to meet
you, Taneo.”
“Likewise.” Taneo shook Joker’s hand, “Is that part of your quirk?”
Joker chuckled as he kicked the ground with his heel, shades of vermilion and purple rippled
from his boot. “Why don’t we save the questions for the interview?”
“Right.” Taneo turned and opened the door, “The rest of the team is inside. They can’t wait to
meet you.”
Joker smiled as a light breeze ruffled his hair, a ‘good luck’ from Mona. Taneo led him
through empty hallways and vacant rooms, before he stood at another door. They stepped into
a larger room with a couch and plush chairs, a coffee table littered with refreshments,

windows on the left side of the room showcased equipment and the live studio itself. They
weren’t alone.
Suddenly, he was rushed by a woman with long hair and eyes as sharp as his dagger.
“Joker!” Her hand jutted out, “I’m so glad we could meet in person. My name is Mitsuo
Chihiro, editor-in-chief for Juzo News!”
Joker shook hands with her, then glanced at the two men behind her. The younger one was
giving Joker a bug eyed look. The other wasn’t as shell shocked, but admiration and awe
lined every part of his body.
“M-my name I-is Yuma Takashi, Joker sir! I’m a big fan!!”
“Minato Haruka. I-it’s nice to meet you. What should we call you?”
“Just Joker.”
Taneo chuckled as Joker shook their hands. Yuma’s soul was about to float out of his body,
and he stared at his hand in a way that suggested he might not ever wash it.
Mitsuo sighed, but there was a playful smile to her lips. “As agreed, Taneo will host the
interview. Yuma, Minato, and I will be in the other room managing the technical side of
things.”
“And one other.” Joker said.
“One other?” Mitsuo furrowed her brows, “Who?”
Joker dug out his phone and sent the text to Aiba. The surrounding speakers buzzed to life
and a familiar voice came through.
“I’m in!”
“Who’re you?” Taneo asked.
“La Brava. I’m going to broadcast this interview all over the country!”
Joker smiled softly, it seems living with Gentle Criminal has already gotten her out of her
shell. And she gained a code name to boot. He was so proud.
Mitsuo turned to Yuma and Minato, “You two start setting up, I’ll be there in a moment!”
“Y-yes ma’am!!” They shouted in unison and darted into the other room.
Mitsuo stared at Joker, her brows furrowed, “Are you sure you don’t want your voice to be
disguised like Taneo’s? It’s going to be even more dangerous for you since your friend is
spreading it all over Japan.”
“Don’t worry,” Joker smirked, “I won’t be the only star of the show.”

Taneo and Mitsuo gasped at the bright flash of blue and smothering heat, Minato and Yuma
pressed their faces into the window to watch. Flames bathed Arsene, casting iridescent colors
on his wings while his eyes smoldered like hell fire.
Joker experienced a wave of smug satisfaction when their jaws hit the floor, Mitsuo was
grinning like a madwoman.
“I am Arsene, the Pillager of Twilight!!” Arsene tipped his hat, “At your service.”
“N-nice to meet you, Arsene.” Taneo stared at Joker, “I don’t understand. What does he have
to do with disguising your voice?”
“I am thou, thou art I.”
Joker and Arsene’s voices harmonized like the unified strings of an orchestra. A violin and
cello with perfect melodies.
“A few of us want our voices to be heard,” Arsene said with a wave of his arm, “And will
partake in this play.”
“I hope you don’t mind.” Joker tilted his head, “I just couldn’t say no to them.”
“The more the merrier!” Mitsuo cackled and rubbed her hands together, “This will be the best
interview of our career, boys!”
Taneo chuckled as he stepped into the next room, Joker and Arsene at his heels.
It was dark, the walls were lined with sound proof pads. Arsene had to duck and fold his
wings to fit through the door, but it was spacious enough for him to stand comfortably as
Joker sank into the closest chair. Taneo adjusted the various microphones and handed him a
headset, then took the chair opposite of Joker. He placed a small notebook on the table and
opened it.
“You ready for this, you two?”
“More than ready.”
Taneo signalled the others, they fiddled with the machinery until Mitsuo gave them a thumbs
up. The green ‘On Air!’ light turned on.

“Good luck.” Aizawa slipped off his goggles, a perfect ring of untouched skin around his
eyes, “I don’t think a dozen and a half showers will ever rid us of the glitter.”
“Or the second media fallout that’s bound to happen over this stunt.” Tsukauchi wanted
nothing more than to go home and collapse in bed, “Let’s just gather up any evidence we can
and get out of here.”
Nezu dropped the stuffed animal and jumped onto Aizawa’s shoulders, covering him with
another layer of glitzy glamour. Aizawa sputtered and almost choked on the cursed stuff.

“Well, this was an interesting turn of events!” Nezu exclaimed, “I certainly had fun, hee ho!”
“Nezu.” Aizawa’s eyes went red and his hair floated amidst a sea of sparkles, “Not. Another.
Word.”
“Oh come on, Eraser!” Midnight bumped shoulders with him, her other hand flicked glitter
right in his face, “Learn to live a little, hee ho!”
“That’s it.”
He shrugged off Midnight, picked up Nezu like the grinning toddler he was and placed him
on the shining table. Aizawa shoved his hands in his pockets and walked out, but not before
he stopped at the door frame.
“I hate all of you.”
Nezu and Midnight’s roaring laughter followed him down the hallway.
This night would irritate him for months, just like the flecks of glitter that trailed behind his
every step.
